+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.layout.test.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,577 @@
+import { act, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { createRef } from 'react';
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import type { Mock } from 'vitest';
+import { resetDevWarnings } from '../../internal/warn';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type {
+  DataGridColumn,
+  DataGridColumnLayout,
+  DataGridHandle,
+  DataGridProps,
+  DataGridSortItem,
+} from './index';
+
+// The layout of the columns (spec phase 6 §6.3 "Cột (Plan C)"): where it starts, what a controlled
+// layout shows, what is dropped without a word, and what a hidden column does to the sort and to the
+// keyboard.
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  // jsdom has no layout, so every element would count as hidden to the code that looks for the
+  // controls of a cell.
+  HTMLElement.prototype.checkVisibility = () => true;
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'checkVisibility');
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  qty: number;
+  total: number;
+}
+
+const ORDERS: Order[] = [
+  { id: 'DH-1030', customer: 'Nguyễn Minh', qty: 4, total: 1250000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1029', customer: 'Trần Hải', qty: 1, total: 890000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1028', customer: 'Lê An', qty: 12, total: 15400000 },
+];
+
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+  { field: 'total', caption: 'Total', dataType: 'number', width: 120 },
+];
+const IDS = ['id', 'customer', 'qty', 'total'];
+
+const layout = (parts: Partial<DataGridColumnLayout> = {}): DataGridColumnLayout => ({
+  order: IDS,
+  widths: { id: 104, customer: 200, qty: 80, total: 120 },
+  hidden: [],
+  pinned: {},
+  ...parts,
+});
+
+function Orders(props: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>> & { gridRef?: React.Ref<DataGridHandle> }) {
+  const { gridRef, ...rest } = props;
+  return (
+    <DataGrid
+      ref={gridRef}
+      data={ORDERS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={false}
+      {...rest}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+const grid = () => screen.getByRole('grid');
+const captions = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll('thead th.flg-data-grid-head'), (th) => th.textContent);
+const bodyRows = () => Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr'));
+const ids = () => bodyRows().map((row) => row.children[0]!.textContent);
+const head = (caption: string) =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('thead th')).find((th) =>
+    th.textContent?.startsWith(caption),
+  )!;
+const widths = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('colgroup > col'), (col) => col.style.width);
+const spyWarn = () => vi.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {});
+const warnings = (warn: Mock) => warn.mock.calls.map(([message]) => String(message));
+
+describe('where the layout starts', () => {
+  it('is the columns as given: their order, widths, pins and the ones that are hidden', () => {
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    render(
+      <Orders
+        gridRef={ref}
+        columns={[
+          COLUMNS[0]!,
+          { ...COLUMNS[1]!, visible: false },
+          { ...COLUMNS[2]!, pinned: 'right' },
+          { ...COLUMNS[3]!, pinned: 'left' },
+        ]}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Total', 'Order', 'Qty']);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().columnLayout).toEqual({
+      order: IDS,
+      widths: { id: 104, customer: 200, qty: 80, total: 120 },
+      hidden: ['customer'],
+      pinned: { qty: 'right', total: 'left' },
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('is the state a grid with no layout says, JSON only', () => {
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    render(<Orders gridRef={ref} />);
+    const state = ref.current!.getState();
+    expect(state.columnLayout).toEqual(layout());
+    expect(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(state))).toEqual(state);
+  });
+
+  // Qty says `visible: false` here: the part a default layout gives replaces the columns' own, whole.
+  const HIDES_QTY = [COLUMNS[0]!, COLUMNS[1]!, { ...COLUMNS[2]!, visible: false }, COLUMNS[3]!];
+
+  it('lets a defaultColumnLayout order replace the order of the columns', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={{ order: ['total', 'id', 'qty', 'customer'] }} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Total', 'Order', 'Qty', 'Customer']);
+  });
+
+  it('lets a defaultColumnLayout hidden replace the columns own visible, in both directions', () => {
+    const { unmount } = render(<Orders columns={HIDES_QTY} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Total']);
+    unmount();
+    render(<Orders columns={HIDES_QTY} defaultColumnLayout={{ hidden: ['total'] }} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty']);
+  });
+
+  it('lets a defaultColumnLayout pinned replace the columns own pins', () => {
+    render(
+      <Orders
+        columns={[{ ...COLUMNS[0]!, pinned: 'right' }, ...COLUMNS.slice(1)]}
+        defaultColumnLayout={{ pinned: { total: 'left' } }}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Total', 'Order', 'Customer', 'Qty']);
+  });
+
+  it('lets a defaultColumnLayout of widths replace the widths of the columns', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={{ widths: { customer: 260, qty: 90 } }} />);
+    // An entry of the layout wins over the own width of its column; a column with no entry keeps it.
+    expect(widths().slice(0, 4)).toEqual(['104px', '260px', '90px', '120px']);
+  });
+
+  it('does not start again from a later defaultColumnLayout, nor from a later change of a column', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={{ hidden: ['qty'] }} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Total']);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders
+        defaultColumnLayout={{ hidden: [] }}
+        columns={[
+          { ...COLUMNS[0]!, visible: false, pinned: 'right' },
+          ...COLUMNS.slice(1, 3),
+          { ...COLUMNS[3]!, width: 300 },
+        ]}
+      />,
+    );
+    // The layout knows every column: their own `visible`, `pinned` and `width` no longer count.
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Total']);
+    expect(widths().slice(0, 3)).toEqual(['104px', '200px', '120px']);
+  });
+
+  it('puts a column the layout does not know at the end of its zone, with its own values', () => {
+    const extra: DataGridColumn<Order> = {
+      field: 'customer',
+      id: 'who',
+      caption: 'Who',
+      width: 90,
+    };
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders gridRef={ref} />);
+    rerender(<Orders gridRef={ref} columns={[...COLUMNS, extra]} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total', 'Who']);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().columnLayout.order).toEqual([...IDS, 'who']);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().columnLayout.widths.who).toBe(90);
+    rerender(<Orders gridRef={ref} columns={[...COLUMNS, { ...extra, pinned: 'left' }]} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Who', 'Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total']);
+    rerender(<Orders gridRef={ref} columns={[...COLUMNS, { ...extra, visible: false }]} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total']);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('a controlled layout', () => {
+  it('shows the layout it is given: the order, the widths, the hidden and the pinned', () => {
+    render(
+      <Orders
+        columnLayout={layout({
+          order: ['total', 'qty', 'customer', 'id'],
+          widths: { total: 150, qty: 70 },
+          hidden: ['customer'],
+          pinned: { id: 'left' },
+        })}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Total', 'Qty']);
+    // Order is pinned and has no entry: it keeps its own width.
+    expect(widths().slice(0, 3)).toEqual(['104px', '150px', '70px']);
+  });
+
+  it('follows the layout when the parent gives another, and calls nothing for it', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const handlers = { onColumnLayoutChange, onStateChange };
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders {...handlers} columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders
+        {...handlers}
+        columnLayout={layout({ order: ['qty', ...IDS.filter((i) => i !== 'qty')] })}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Qty', 'Order', 'Customer', 'Total']);
+    rerender(<Orders {...handlers} columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['id'] })} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Customer', 'Qty', 'Total']);
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    expect(onStateChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('gives getState the layout as shown: new columns appended, gone ids dropped, widths held', () => {
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    render(
+      <Orders
+        gridRef={ref}
+        columnLayout={{
+          order: ['total', 'gone', 'id', 'qty'],
+          widths: { total: 9000, qty: 10, gone: 50 },
+          hidden: ['gone'],
+          pinned: { gone: 'left', id: 'right' },
+        }}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().columnLayout).toEqual({
+      order: ['total', 'id', 'qty', 'customer'],
+      widths: { id: 104, total: 2000, qty: 60, customer: 200 },
+      hidden: [],
+      pinned: { id: 'right' },
+    });
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Total', 'Qty', 'Customer', 'Order']);
+  });
+
+  it('says nothing about what a saved layout may hold: ids of no column, repeats, bad pins and widths', () => {
+    const warn = spyWarn();
+    render(
+      <Orders
+        columnLayout={{
+          order: ['id', 'id', 'flg:select', 'nope', 'customer', 'qty', 'total'],
+          widths: { nope: 50, id: 5, customer: 99999 },
+          hidden: ['nope', 'nope'],
+          pinned: { nope: 'left', id: 'top', qty: 7 } as never,
+        }}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total']);
+    expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('shows the first column in the order when every column is hidden', () => {
+    const warn = spyWarn();
+    render(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ order: ['qty', ...IDS], hidden: IDS })} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Qty']);
+    expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('shows no column for no column, and does not throw', () => {
+    render(<Orders columns={[]} columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['id'] })} />);
+    expect(captions()).toEqual([]);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('props of a shape the types forbid', () => {
+  const bad = (value: unknown) => value as never;
+
+  it.each(['columnLayout', 'defaultColumnLayout'])(
+    'uses a %s that is not an object as none, and warns once',
+    (prop) => {
+      const warn = spyWarn();
+      const { rerender } = render(<Orders {...{ [prop]: bad('wide') }} />);
+      rerender(<Orders {...{ [prop]: bad(7) }} />);
+      expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total']);
+      expect(warnings(warn)).toEqual([expect.stringContaining(`${prop} is not an object`)]);
+    },
+  );
+
+  it.each(['columnLayout', 'defaultColumnLayout'] as const)(
+    'uses the safe part for each part of %s of the wrong kind, and warns once for the prop',
+    (prop) => {
+      const warn = spyWarn();
+      render(
+        <Orders
+          {...{
+            [prop]: bad({
+              order: 'id,customer',
+              widths: [100, 200],
+              hidden: [3, 'qty', null],
+              pinned: 'left',
+            }),
+          }}
+        />,
+      );
+      // `order` is empty, so every column is new and has its own values, `hidden` and all: a default
+      // layout is another matter, where the strings of `hidden` are the columns that start hidden.
+      expect(captions()).toEqual(
+        prop === 'columnLayout'
+          ? ['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total']
+          : ['Order', 'Customer', 'Total'],
+      );
+      expect(warnings(warn)).toEqual([expect.stringContaining(`${prop} is not an object`)]);
+    },
+  );
+
+  it('warns for a width that is not a number, and drops that entry', () => {
+    const warn = spyWarn();
+    render(<Orders columnLayout={bad({ ...layout(), widths: { id: '104', customer: 150 } })} />);
+    expect(widths().slice(0, 2)).toEqual(['104px', '150px']);
+    expect(warnings(warn)).toEqual([expect.stringContaining('columnLayout is not an object')]);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps a layout of its shape as it came, so nothing is done again for it', () => {
+    const given = layout();
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders gridRef={ref} columnLayout={given} />);
+    const shown = ref.current!.getState().columnLayout;
+    rerender(<Orders gridRef={ref} columnLayout={given} />);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().columnLayout).toBe(shown);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the shown layout while an inline layout says the same', () => {
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders gridRef={ref} columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    const shown = ref.current!.getState().columnLayout;
+    rerender(<Orders gridRef={ref} columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().columnLayout).toBe(shown);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('a column that is hidden', () => {
+  const SORT: DataGridSortItem[] = [
+    { field: 'qty', direction: 'desc' },
+    { field: 'customer', direction: 'asc' },
+  ];
+  const buttonName = (caption: string) => head(caption).querySelector('button')!;
+
+  it('sorts nothing: the rows follow the next level, and the state keeps its item', () => {
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    const { rerender } = render(
+      <Orders gridRef={ref} defaultSort={SORT} columnLayout={layout()} />,
+    );
+    // Quantities 12, 4, 1.
+    expect(ids()).toEqual(['DH-1028', 'DH-1030', 'DH-1029']);
+    expect(buttonName('Customer')).toHaveAccessibleName('Customer, sorted ascending, 2 of 2');
+
+    rerender(
+      <Orders gridRef={ref} defaultSort={SORT} columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['qty'] })} />,
+    );
+    // The customers are Lê An, Nguyễn Minh, Trần Hải.
+    expect(ids()).toEqual(['DH-1028', 'DH-1030', 'DH-1029']);
+    expect(head('Customer')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');
+    // One level is shown, so there is nothing to number: no "2" without a "1".
+    expect(buttonName('Customer')).toHaveAccessibleName('Customer');
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().sort).toEqual(SORT);
+
+    rerender(<Orders gridRef={ref} defaultSort={SORT} columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    expect(ids()).toEqual(['DH-1028', 'DH-1030', 'DH-1029']);
+    expect(head('Qty')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'descending');
+    expect(buttonName('Customer')).toHaveAccessibleName('Customer, sorted ascending, 2 of 2');
+  });
+
+  it('gives the rows the order of the level that is shown', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(
+      <Orders
+        defaultSort={[
+          { field: 'qty', direction: 'asc' },
+          { field: 'total', direction: 'desc' },
+        ]}
+        columnLayout={layout()}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(ids()).toEqual(['DH-1029', 'DH-1030', 'DH-1028']);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders
+        defaultSort={[
+          { field: 'qty', direction: 'asc' },
+          { field: 'total', direction: 'desc' },
+        ]}
+        columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['qty'] })}
+      />,
+    );
+    // By total, descending: 15.4M, 1.25M, 0.89M.
+    expect(ids()).toEqual(['DH-1028', 'DH-1030', 'DH-1029']);
+    expect(head('Total')).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'descending');
+  });
+
+  it('does not sort again when only the order of the columns changes', () => {
+    const sortValue = vi.fn((row: Order) => row.qty);
+    const columns: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+      COLUMNS[0]!,
+      { ...COLUMNS[2]!, sortValue },
+      COLUMNS[1]!,
+    ];
+    const defaultSort: DataGridSortItem[] = [{ field: 'qty', direction: 'asc' }];
+    const { rerender } = render(
+      <Orders
+        columns={columns}
+        defaultSort={defaultSort}
+        columnLayout={layout({ order: ['id', 'qty', 'customer'] })}
+      />,
+    );
+    const calls = sortValue.mock.calls.length;
+    expect(calls).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders
+        columns={columns}
+        defaultSort={defaultSort}
+        columnLayout={layout({ order: ['qty', 'id', 'customer'] })}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Qty', 'Order', 'Customer']);
+    expect(sortValue.mock.calls.length).toBe(calls);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('the keyboard when the columns change', () => {
+  const stops = () => Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[tabindex="0"]'));
+  const focusOn = (element: HTMLElement) => act(() => element.focus());
+
+  it('keeps the place on its column when the column moves', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    const qty = bodyRows()[1]!.children[2] as HTMLElement;
+    focusOn(qty);
+    expect(stops()).toEqual([qty]);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ order: ['qty', 'id', 'customer', 'total'] })} />);
+    expect(stops()).toEqual([bodyRows()[1]!.children[0]]);
+    expect(stops()[0]!.textContent).toBe('1');
+  });
+
+  it('moves the place of a column that is hidden to the column now at its index', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    focusOn(bodyRows()[1]!.children[1] as HTMLElement);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['customer'] })} />);
+    // Customer was the second column; Qty is now the second.
+    expect(stops()).toEqual([bodyRows()[1]!.children[1]]);
+    expect(stops()[0]!.textContent).toBe('1');
+    // And again, from the last column: the place goes to the new last one.
+    focusOn(bodyRows()[1]!.children[2] as HTMLElement);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['customer', 'total'] })} />);
+    expect(stops()).toEqual([bodyRows()[1]!.children[1]]);
+    expect(stops()[0]!.textContent).toBe('1');
+  });
+
+  it('moves the place of a title that is hidden the same way', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    focusOn(head('Customer'));
+    expect(stops()).toEqual([head('Customer')]);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['customer'] })} />);
+    expect(stops()).toEqual([head('Qty')]);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['customer', 'qty', 'total'] })} />);
+    expect(stops()).toEqual([head('Order')]);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the focus on the cell when a new layout moves its column', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    const qty = bodyRows()[0]!.children[2] as HTMLElement;
+    focusOn(qty);
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(qty);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ order: ['qty', 'id', 'customer', 'total'] })} />);
+    const now = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
+    expect(grid().contains(now)).toBe(true);
+    expect(now).toBe(bodyRows()[0]!.children[0]);
+    expect(now.textContent).toBe('4');
+    expect(now).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '0');
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the focus in the grid when the column it is on is hidden', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    focusOn(bodyRows()[0]!.children[1] as HTMLElement);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['customer'] })} />);
+    expect(grid().contains(document.activeElement)).toBe(true);
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(bodyRows()[0]!.children[1]);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the focus on a title when its column moves', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    focusOn(head('Total'));
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ order: ['total', 'id', 'customer', 'qty'] })} />);
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(head('Total'));
+  });
+
+  it('goes on from the column the place is on, wherever it is now: ArrowRight is the next on the screen', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    const first = bodyRows()[0]!.children[0] as HTMLElement;
+    focusOn(first);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ order: ['qty', 'id', 'customer', 'total'] })} />);
+    const event = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {
+      key: 'ArrowRight',
+      bubbles: true,
+      cancelable: true,
+    });
+    act(() => {
+      document.activeElement!.dispatchEvent(event);
+    });
+    // The place is on Order, which is the second column now, so the next one is Customer.
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(bodyRows()[0]!.children[2]);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('a column whose own values change after the layout started', () => {
+  const MESSAGE = 'only start the column layout';
+  const withColumn = (index: number, extra: Partial<DataGridColumn<Order>>) =>
+    COLUMNS.map((column, at) =>
+      at === index ? ({ ...column, ...extra } as typeof column) : column,
+    );
+
+  it.each([
+    ['visible', { visible: false }],
+    ['width', { width: 150 }],
+    ['pinned', { pinned: 'left' as const }],
+  ])('warns once for a changed %s, whether the layout is held or given', (_name, extra) => {
+    const warn = spyWarn();
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    rerender(<Orders columns={withColumn(1, extra)} />);
+    rerender(<Orders columns={withColumn(1, { ...extra, caption: 'Again' })} />);
+    expect(warnings(warn)).toEqual([expect.stringContaining(MESSAGE)]);
+    expect(warnings(warn)[0]).not.toContain('customer');
+    warn.mockClear();
+    resetDevWarnings();
+    const controlled = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} />);
+    controlled.rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout()} columns={withColumn(1, extra)} />);
+    expect(warnings(warn)).toEqual([expect.stringContaining(MESSAGE)]);
+  });
+
+  it('says nothing for a columns array written inline with the same values', () => {
+    const warn = spyWarn();
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columns={withColumn(1, { visible: true })} />);
+    rerender(<Orders columns={withColumn(1, { visible: true })} />);
+    rerender(<Orders columns={COLUMNS.map((column) => ({ ...column }))} />);
+    expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('says nothing when the new value is what the shown layout already has', () => {
+    const warn = spyWarn();
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['customer'] })} />);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders
+        columnLayout={layout({ hidden: ['customer'] })}
+        columns={withColumn(1, { visible: false, width: 200 })}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('says nothing for a column that is new', () => {
+    const warn = spyWarn();
+    const extra: DataGridColumn<Order> = { field: 'customer', id: 'who', width: 90 };
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+    rerender(<Orders columns={[...COLUMNS, extra]} />);
+    rerender(<Orders columns={[...COLUMNS, { ...extra, visible: false }]} />);
+    // The layout does not know it yet, so its own values still apply: nothing is ignored.
+    expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('does no work in production', () => {
+    vi.stubEnv('NODE_ENV', 'production');
+    try {
+      const warn = spyWarn();
+      const { rerender } = render(<Orders />);
+      rerender(<Orders columns={withColumn(1, { visible: false })} />);
+      expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    } finally {
+      vi.unstubAllEnvs();
+    }
+  });
+});

+const column = (id: string, extra: Partial<ResolvedColumn<Row>> = {}): ResolvedColumn<Row> => ({
+  id,

+  ownText: false,

+});

+describe('startLayout', () => {
+  it('is the order of the array, with the own hidden, pinned and width of the columns', () => {
+    const columns = [
+      column('a', { width: 100 }),

+      column('c', { pinned: 'right', width: 80 }),
+      column('d', { pinned: 'left' }),
+    ];
+    expect(startLayout(columns)).toEqual({
+      order: ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'],
+      widths: { a: 100, c: 80 },
+      hidden: ['b'],
+      pinned: { c: 'right', d: 'left' },
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('is empty for no column', () => {
+    expect(startLayout([])).toEqual(EMPTY);
+  });
+
+  const own = { order: ['a', 'b'], widths: { a: 100 }, hidden: ['b'], pinned: { a: 'left' } };
+  it.each([
+    ['order', { order: ['b', 'a'] }],
+    ['widths', { widths: { b: 70 } }],
+    ['hidden', { hidden: [] }],
+    ['pinned', { pinned: { b: 'right' } }],
+  ] as const)('lets a given %s replace that part and no other', (name, given) => {
+    const columns = [column('a', { width: 100, pinned: 'left' }), column('b', { visible: false })];

+    expect(name in given).toBe(true);

+  it('takes a part that is undefined for no part', () => {

+    expect(ids(applied)).toEqual(['c', 'a', 'b']);
+    expect(applied.columns[0]).toBe(abc[2]);
+    expect(applied.columns[1]).toBe(abc[0]);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the zones in order: the left, the middle, then the right, each in `order`', () => {
+    const applied = applyLayout(
+      abc.concat(column('d'), column('e')),

+      }),

+  const copy = (): DataGridColumnLayout => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(one)) as DataGridColumnLayout;
+
+  it('says that two layouts with the same parts are the same, by value', () => {
+    expect(sameLayout(one, copy())).toBe(true);

+import { act, renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import type { DataGridColumnLayout, DataGridState } from '../types';
+import { useGridState } from './use-grid-state';
+import type { GridStateOptions } from './use-grid-state';
+
+// The layout of the columns is a controllable triple like the others: the setter calls
+// `onColumnLayoutChange` and then `onStateChange` with the shown state (spec phase 6 §6.1). Nothing
+// of the grid asks for a layout yet, so it is the hook that is tested.
+
+const layout = (parts: Partial<DataGridColumnLayout> = {}): DataGridColumnLayout => ({
+  order: ['a', 'b', 'c'],
+  widths: {},
+  hidden: [],
+  pinned: {},
+  ...parts,
+});
+
+const SHOWN: DataGridState = {
+  sort: [],
+  page: { index: 0, size: 20 },
+  selectedKeys: [],
+  columnLayout: layout(),
+};
+
+function options(extra: Partial<GridStateOptions> = {}): GridStateOptions {
+  return {
+    sort: undefined,
+    defaultSort: undefined,
+    onSortChange: undefined,
+    page: undefined,
+    defaultPage: { index: 0, size: 20 },
+    onPageChange: undefined,
+    selectedKeys: undefined,
+    defaultSelectedKeys: undefined,
+    onSelectedKeysChange: undefined,
+    columnLayout: undefined,
+    defaultColumnLayout: layout(),
+    onColumnLayoutChange: undefined,
+    onStateChange: undefined,
+    shown: { current: SHOWN },
+    ...extra,
+  };
+}
+
+describe('the layout of the columns in useGridState', () => {
+  it('starts from the default layout, and holds the one that is asked for while uncontrolled', () => {
+    const { result } = renderHook(() => useGridState(options()));
+    expect(result.current.state.columnLayout).toEqual(layout());
+    const next = layout({ order: ['c', 'b', 'a'] });
+    act(() => result.current.setColumnLayout(next));
+    expect(result.current.state.columnLayout).toBe(next);
+  });
+
+  it('reports a layout to onColumnLayoutChange and then to onStateChange, with the shown state', () => {
+    const calls: string[] = [];
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn(() => void calls.push('layout'));
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn(() => void calls.push('state'));
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ onColumnLayoutChange, onStateChange })),
+    );
+    const next = layout({ hidden: ['b'] });
+    act(() => result.current.setColumnLayout(next));
+    expect(calls).toEqual(['layout', 'state']);
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(next);
+    expect(onStateChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(
+      { ...SHOWN, columnLayout: next },
+      'columnLayout',
+    );
+  });
+
+  it('sends the state the grid shows, with the layout asked for on top', () => {
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const shown = {
+      current: {
+        ...SHOWN,
+        sort: [{ field: 'a', direction: 'asc' as const }],
+        page: { index: 3, size: 5 },
+      },
+    };
+    const { result } = renderHook(() => useGridState(options({ onStateChange, shown })));
+    act(() => result.current.setColumnLayout(layout({ order: ['b', 'a', 'c'] })));
+    const [state] = onStateChange.mock.calls[0] as [DataGridState];
+    expect(state.sort).toEqual([{ field: 'a', direction: 'asc' }]);
+    expect(state.page).toEqual({ index: 3, size: 5 });
+    expect(state.columnLayout.order).toEqual(['b', 'a', 'c']);
+  });
+
+  it('reports nothing for a layout that says what the grid shows already, though it is a new object', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ onColumnLayoutChange, onStateChange })),
+    );
+    act(() => result.current.setColumnLayout(layout()));
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    expect(onStateChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('reports each of two requests made before a render, the second against the first', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ onColumnLayoutChange, onStateChange })),
+    );
+    const first = layout({ hidden: ['a'] });
+    const second = layout({ hidden: ['a', 'b'] });
+    act(() => {
+      result.current.setColumnLayout(first);
+      result.current.setColumnLayout(first);
+      result.current.setColumnLayout(second);
+    });
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange.mock.calls).toEqual([[first], [second]]);
+    expect(onStateChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
+    expect(result.current.state.columnLayout).toBe(second);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps a controlled layout the parent does not take, and still reports the request', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const held = layout();
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ columnLayout: held, onColumnLayoutChange, onStateChange })),
+    );
+    const next = layout({ order: ['b', 'a', 'c'] });
+    act(() => result.current.setColumnLayout(next));
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(next);
+    expect(onStateChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(
+      { ...SHOWN, columnLayout: next },
+      'columnLayout',
+    );
+    expect(result.current.state.columnLayout).toBe(held);
+    // The parent that keeps its layout is asked again for the same request.
+    act(() => result.current.setColumnLayout(next));
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
+  });
+
+  it('follows a controlled layout the parent takes, and calls nothing for it', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const { result, rerender } = renderHook(
+      (columnLayout: DataGridColumnLayout) =>
+        useGridState(options({ columnLayout, onColumnLayoutChange, onStateChange })),
+      { initialProps: layout() },
+    );
+    const next = layout({ order: ['c', 'a', 'b'] });
+    rerender(next);
+    expect(result.current.state.columnLayout).toBe(next);
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    expect(onStateChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('leaves the other parts of the state as they are', () => {
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ defaultSort: [{ field: 'b', direction: 'desc' }] })),
+    );
+    act(() => result.current.setColumnLayout(layout({ order: ['c', 'b', 'a'] })));
+    expect(result.current.state.sort).toEqual([{ field: 'b', direction: 'desc' }]);
+    expect(result.current.state.page).toEqual({ index: 0, size: 20 });
+  });
+});

+import { renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+import { sameList, sameMembers, useKept } from './use-kept';
+
+describe('sameList and sameMembers', () => {
+  const a = { id: 'a' };
+  const b = { id: 'b' };
+
+  it('compare the items by identity, in order or in any order', () => {
+    expect(sameList([a, b], [a, b])).toBe(true);
+    expect(sameList([a, b], [b, a])).toBe(false);
+    expect(sameList([a], [a, b])).toBe(false);
+    expect(sameList([a, { id: 'b' }], [a, b])).toBe(false);
+    expect(sameMembers([a, b], [b, a])).toBe(true);
+    expect(sameMembers([a, b], [a])).toBe(false);
+    expect(sameMembers([a, a], [a, b])).toBe(false);
+    expect(sameList([], [])).toBe(true);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('useKept', () => {
+  const sameId = (kept: { id: number }, next: { id: number }) => kept.id === next.id;
+
+  it('gives back the value of an earlier render while the new one says the same', () => {
+    const first = { id: 1 };
+    const { result, rerender } = renderHook((value: { id: number }) => useKept(value, sameId), {
+      initialProps: first,
+    });
+    expect(result.current).toBe(first);
+    rerender({ id: 1 });
+    expect(result.current).toBe(first);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the new value once it differs, and goes on from it', () => {
+    const { result, rerender } = renderHook((value: { id: number }) => useKept(value, sameId), {
+      initialProps: { id: 1 },
+    });
+    const second = { id: 2 };
+    rerender(second);
+    expect(result.current).toBe(second);
+    rerender({ id: 2 });
+    expect(result.current).toBe(second);
+  });
+});

 **Mô hình focus** (mẫu data grid của APG):
 
 - **Một điểm Tab.** Đúng một phần tử trong bảng có `tabindex="0"`: ô đang hoạt động (hay hàng nhóm đang hoạt động, hay control duy nhất của ô, bên dưới); mọi ô khác và mọi control trong ô `tabindex="-1"`. Thanh công cụ, thanh lưu, thanh bộ lọc và thanh phân trang là các điểm Tab riêng trước và sau bảng. Khung cuộn mang `tabindex="-1"` cố định (không bao giờ đổi, không có `role`): Firefox đưa một phần tử cuộn được vào thứ tự Tab nếu nó không có `tabindex`, kể cả khi trong nó đã có ô là điểm Tab; `-1` giữ khung ngoài thứ tự Tab mà vẫn không bị gỡ khi đang giữ focus (phát hiện khi lập Plan B). Control trong ô tuỳ biến (`cell`) được grid đặt `tabindex="-1"` sau mỗi lần commit, nhớ giá trị cũ của từng cái và trả đúng giá trị đó khi grid biến mất; nút sắp xếp ở tiêu đề cũng vậy (phát hiện khi lập Plan B). Control mà ô tự thêm khi render riêng (không có commit nào của grid: link đến sau một lần tải, `Suspense` xong) cũng được đặt `-1`, qua một `MutationObserver` (`childList`, `subtree`) trên `<tbody>`, chỉ có khi grid có cột `cell` và gỡ khi không còn; observer đó cũng nghe `attributes` (`attributeFilter`: `disabled`, `tabindex`, `href`, `contenteditable`, `hidden`, `inert`), nên control mà ô làm thành điểm Tab bằng một thuộc tính (nút ô tự bật sau một lần tải, link có `href`, `tabindex` roving mà ô tự chuyển) cũng được đặt `-1`; observer chỉ xem các ô của bảng mà bản ghi nằm trong và các dòng được thêm vào (cửa sổ dời, dòng đến), không đi lại cả `<tbody>` (vòng sửa thứ hai); bản ghi của chính các lần ghi của grid được lấy đi bằng `takeRecords()` ngay sau khi ghi (lần ghi là đồng bộ, nên không lấy mất gì khác), nên observer không đọc chúng và không chạy lại; một `tabindex` ô ghi sau grid là của ô: giá trị từ 0 trở lên được lấy lại cùng giá trị mới để trả, giá trị âm ở nguyên và không được trả khi grid biến mất (phát hiện khi review PR #42); control nằm trong popup của ô (`[popover]`, `dialog`) giữ nguyên `tabindex` của nó, vì popup là chỗ riêng như với phím và lần nhấn; cả hai qua một hook `use-release-controls.ts` mà nút ở tiêu đề của C và trình sửa của F dùng lại (phát hiện khi review cuối Plan B).
-- **Vị trí hoạt động** lưu bằng (khoá dòng hoặc khoá nhóm, id cột), không bằng chỉ số DOM, nên sắp xếp, lọc, cuộn ảo không làm mất chỗ. Lúc đầu: ô đầu của dòng thân đầu tiên (không có dòng: ô tiêu đề đầu). Dòng hoạt động biến mất (lọc, xoá) thì vị trí chuyển sang dòng cùng chỉ số (kẹp lại), và nếu focus đang ở trong grid thì focus theo sang đó ("trong grid" là trong DOM của bảng: sự kiện focus của một portal mà ô mở, như popover của thư viện ngoài, đi qua bảng trong cây React nhưng không tính, nên focus trong portal không bị kéo về ô hoạt động khi grid render lại; phát hiện khi review cuối Plan B).  - **Ô chỉ có một control đơn giản** (ô chọn của cột chọn dòng, ô chọn tất cả ở tiêu đề, nút mở chi tiết, tay nắm kéo dòng): chính control đó là đích của focus (APG), Space/Enter tác động thẳng lên nó. Đích của ô hoạt động đổi trong lúc focus ở trong ô (ô chọn ở tiêu đề bật lên khi dòng đến lúc ô tiêu đề đang giữ focus, hay tắt đi khi dòng hết lúc chính nó giữ focus) thì sau lần commit đó focus sang đích mới (`preventScroll`), vì phím được đọc từ đích; cả ba engine giữ focus trên control vừa bị tắt ít nhất một khung hình rồi mới đưa nó về `<body>`, nên lần commit kịp chuyển nó (phát hiện khi review PR #42).

 A text that is longer than its cell ends in an ellipsis and does not make its row taller; a screen
 reader still reads all of it. There is no tooltip for a cut text.
 
+## Column layout
+
+The layout of the columns is four parts, each keyed by column id: `order`, `widths` (pixels),
+`hidden` and `pinned` (`'left'` or `'right'`). It is state like the sort: `columnLayout`,
+`defaultColumnLayout` and `onColumnLayoutChange` are a controlled or an uncontrolled value, it is
+part of the state `onStateChange` sends (`changed` is `'columnLayout'`) and of `getState()`, and it
+holds only what JSON can carry, so it can go to `localStorage` and come back as
+`defaultColumnLayout`.
+
+```tsx
+<DataGrid
+  data={orders}
+  rowKey="id"
+  columns={columns}
+  defaultColumnLayout={saved?.columnLayout}
+  onStateChange={(state, changed) => {
+    if (changed === 'columnLayout') save(state.columnLayout);
+  }}
+/>
+```
+
+**Where a layout starts.** The order of the `columns` array, the columns that say `visible: false`
+hidden, their `pinned` and their `width`. `defaultColumnLayout` gives any of the four parts, and a
+part it gives replaces that part whole; the others stay as the columns say. After that the layout is
+the grid's: it is never started again, and a later change of a column's `visible`, `pinned` or place
+in the array does nothing to a column the layout already holds. In development the grid warns once
+when such a change is ignored; change `columnLayout`, or remount the grid with a `key`, instead.
+
+**Known and new columns.** A column whose id is in `order` is laid out by the layout alone: its own
+`visible` and `pinned` no longer count, and its own `width` counts only while `widths` has no entry
+for it. A column that is not in `order` is new (you added it after the layout was saved): it goes
+to the end of its zone, with its own values. A width from the layout is held to `minWidth` and 2000
+pixels, with one exception: the own `width` of a column is always allowed, even under its
+`minWidth`.
+
+**Zones.** The shown columns are the left zone, then the middle, then the right zone, each in the
+order of `order`. The selection column of `selectionMode="multiple"` is no part of the layout: it is
+always first.
+
+**Hidden columns.** A hidden column is not in the DOM and is no column of the grid for the keyboard
+or the sort. At least one column is always shown: a layout that hides every column shows the first
+in `order`. A hidden column sorts nothing, but its item stays in `sort` and in `getState()`: show
+the column again and its level is back, with its number. The next press on a title builds on the
+levels that are shown, so it drops the hidden item.
+
+**What is shown.** `getState().columnLayout`, and the layout that `onColumnLayoutChange` and
+`onStateChange` receive, are the layout as it is shown: the new columns appended, the ids of no
+column dropped, the widths held, and the columns' own widths included for every column that has one.
+A controlled layout you do not take stays as it was, and the callback still hears the request.
+
+**What is cleaned without a word.** A layout may come from the storage of an end user, so these say
+nothing: ids of no column (and `flg:` ids), ids that are repeated, pins that are neither `'left'` nor
+`'right'`, and widths that are out of range or are not a positive number. What its type forbids does
+warn once for the prop, in development: a layout that is not an object, an `order` or `hidden` that
+is not an array of strings, `widths` or `pinned` that are not objects, a width that is not a number.
+The grid uses what it can: an empty part of a controlled layout, no part of a default one.
+
+The keyboard follows a column that moves: the active cell stays on its column. When its column is
+hidden or removed, the active cell goes to the column now at the same place, as it does for a row.
+
+A layout written in the JSX (`columnLayout={{ … }}`) is kept while it says the same, so it draws no
+row again, and a change of a width draws no row and no title.
+

--- a/src/components/data-grid/engine/layout.ts
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/engine/layout.ts
@@ -1,3 +1,7 @@
+import { clamp, isPositive } from '../../../internal/number';
+import type { DataGridColumnLayout, DataGridPin } from '../types';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from './columns';

+
+/** The widest a column may be, in pixels: what a layout, a drag and a key are held to. */
+export const MAX_COLUMN_WIDTH = 2000;
+
+const isPin = (value: unknown): value is DataGridPin => value === 'left' || value === 'right';
+
+/**
+ * The layout a grid starts with: the order of the array, the columns that say `visible: false`
+ * hidden, the pins and the widths they say. Each part that `given` (`defaultColumnLayout`) has
+ * replaces that part, whole, and no other.
+ */
+export function startLayout<TRow>(
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+  given?: Partial<DataGridColumnLayout>,
+): DataGridColumnLayout {
+  const widths: Record<string, number> = {};
+  const pinned: Record<string, DataGridPin> = {};
+  for (const column of columns) {
+    if (column.width !== undefined) widths[column.id] = column.width;
+    if (column.pinned !== undefined) pinned[column.id] = column.pinned;
+  }
+  return {
+    order: given?.order ?? columns.map((column) => column.id),
+    widths: given?.widths ?? widths,
+    hidden: given?.hidden ?? columns.flatMap((column) => (column.visible ? [] : [column.id])),
+    pinned: given?.pinned ?? pinned,
+  };
+}
+
+/** The columns a layout shows, and the layout as they are shown. */
+export interface AppliedLayout<TRow> {
+  /** The shown data columns in zone order: the left zone, the middle, the right zone. */
+  columns: ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  /** The zone of each of `columns`: `undefined` for the middle. */
+  pins: (DataGridPin | undefined)[];
+  /** The width of each of `columns` in pixels, `undefined` for a flexible column. */
+  widths: (number | undefined)[];
+  /**
+   * The layout as shown: `order` with the columns it did not know appended in array order, ids of
+   * no column and repeated ids dropped, `hidden` and `pinned` cleaned the same way, and `widths`
+   * clamped, with the own width of every column that has one and no entry.
+   */
+  layout: DataGridColumnLayout;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Lays the columns out by a layout (spec phase 6 §3.5, §6.3). A column whose id is in `order` is
+ * laid out by the layout alone: its own `visible` and `pinned` no longer count, and its own `width`
+ * only while `widths` has no entry. A column that is not in `order` is new, and goes to the end of
+ * its zone with its own values. A layout may come from the end user's storage, so what does not fit
+ * is dropped without a word: ids of no column (the grid's own `flg:` ids are none), repeated ids,
+ * pins that are no pin, widths that are no positive number; a width is held to the column's
+ * `minWidth` and to 2000, unless it is the column's own width, which a column is always allowed. A
+ * layout that hides every column shows the first in `order`. The `ResolvedColumn` objects are the
+ * ones given, so a new layout builds no column again.
+ */
+export function applyLayout<TRow>(
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+  layout: DataGridColumnLayout,
+): AppliedLayout<TRow> {
+  const byId = new Map(columns.map((column) => [column.id, column]));
+  const known = new Set<string>();
+  const order: string[] = [];
+  for (const id of layout.order) {
+    if (!byId.has(id) || known.has(id)) continue;
+    known.add(id);
+    order.push(id);
+  }
+  const added = columns.filter((column) => !known.has(column.id));
+  for (const column of added) order.push(column.id);
+  const isNew = new Set(added.map((column) => column.id));
+
+  const hiddenIds = new Set<string>();
+  const pins = new Map<string, DataGridPin>();
+  const widths = new Map<string, number>();
+  for (const id of order) {
+    const column = byId.get(id)!;
+    if (isNew.has(id)) {
+      if (!column.visible) hiddenIds.add(id);
+      if (column.pinned !== undefined) pins.set(id, column.pinned);
+      if (column.width !== undefined) widths.set(id, column.width);
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (layout.hidden.includes(id)) hiddenIds.add(id);
+    const pin = layout.pinned[id];
+    if (isPin(pin)) pins.set(id, pin);
+    const width = layout.widths[id];
+    if (isPositive(width)) {
+      widths.set(
+        id,
+        width === column.width ? width : clamp(width, column.minWidth, MAX_COLUMN_WIDTH),
+      );
+    } else if (column.width !== undefined) {
+      widths.set(id, column.width);
+    }
+  }
+  // At least one column is shown: the first in `order` when the layout hides them all.
+  if (order.length > 0 && hiddenIds.size === order.length) hiddenIds.delete(order[0]!);
+
+  const zone = (pin: DataGridPin | undefined) =>
+    order.filter((id) => pins.get(id) === pin && !hiddenIds.has(id));
+  const shown = [...zone('left'), ...zone(undefined), ...zone('right')];
+  return {
+    columns: shown.map((id) => byId.get(id)!),
+    pins: shown.map((id) => pins.get(id)),
+    widths: shown.map((id) => widths.get(id)),
+    layout: {
+      order,
+      widths: Object.fromEntries(
+        order.flatMap((id) => (widths.has(id) ? [[id, widths.get(id)!]] : [])),
+      ),
+      hidden: order.filter((id) => hiddenIds.has(id)),
+      pinned: Object.fromEntries(
+        order.flatMap((id) => (pins.has(id) ? [[id, pins.get(id)!]] : [])),
+      ),
+    },
+  };
+}
+
+/**
+ * `order` with `id` just `before` or `after` `target`; the other ids, the hidden ones too, keep
+ * their places. A new array always, with the same ids in the same order when nothing can move (an
+ * id that is not there, a column onto itself, a column that is already there).
+ */
+export function moveColumn(
+  order: readonly string[],
+  id: string,
+  target: string,
+  side: 'before' | 'after',
+): string[] {
+  if (id === target || !order.includes(id) || !order.includes(target)) return [...order];
+  const rest = order.filter((other) => other !== id);
+  rest.splice(rest.indexOf(target) + (side === 'after' ? 1 : 0), 0, id);
+  return rest;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The layout with a column pinned to `side`, or unpinned (`null`). Pinned, it goes to the end of the
+ * left zone or the start of the right one; unpinned, to the start of the middle (from the left) or
+ * its end (from the right), which are the same two places seen from the other side (spec §6.3
+ * "Ghim"). The zones are in the order of `order`, so the order is put into zone order first; the
+ * layout given when there is nothing to do (an unpin of a column that is not pinned, an unknown id).
+ */
+export function pinColumn(
+  layout: DataGridColumnLayout,
+  id: string,
+  side: DataGridPin | null,
+): DataGridColumnLayout {
+  const was = layout.pinned[id];
+  if (!layout.order.includes(id) || (side === null && !isPin(was))) return layout;
+  const pinned = { ...layout.pinned };
+  if (side === null) delete pinned[id];
+  else pinned[id] = side;
+  const rest = layout.order.filter((other) => other !== id);
+  const zone = (pin: DataGridPin | undefined) =>
+    rest.filter((other) => (isPin(pinned[other]) ? pinned[other] : undefined) === pin);
+  const left = zone('left');
+  const middle = zone(undefined);
+  const right = zone('right');
+  const toTheLeft = (side ?? was) === 'left';
+  return {
+    ...layout,
+    pinned,
+    order: toTheLeft ? [...left, id, ...middle, ...right] : [...left, ...middle, id, ...right],
+  };
+}
+
+/** The layout with `id` hidden or shown; the layout given when that changes nothing. */
+export function setHidden(
+  layout: DataGridColumnLayout,
+  id: string,
+  hidden: boolean,
+): DataGridColumnLayout {
+  if (layout.hidden.includes(id) === hidden) return layout;
+  return {
+    ...layout,
+    hidden: hidden ? [...layout.hidden, id] : layout.hidden.filter((other) => other !== id),
+  };
+}
+
+function sameRecord<T>(a: Readonly<Record<string, T>>, b: Readonly<Record<string, T>>): boolean {
+  const keys = Object.keys(a);
+  return keys.length === Object.keys(b).length && keys.every((key) => a[key] === b[key]);
+}
+
+/** Whether two layouts say the same, each part by value; `hidden` is a set, the rest are not. */
+export function sameLayout(a: DataGridColumnLayout, b: DataGridColumnLayout): boolean {
+  return (
+    a.order.length === b.order.length &&
+    a.order.every((id, index) => id === b.order[index]) &&
+    a.hidden.length === b.hidden.length &&
+    a.hidden.every((id) => b.hidden.includes(id)) &&
+    sameRecord(a.widths, b.widths) &&
+    sameRecord(a.pinned, b.pinned)

+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-start-warning.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-start-warning.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d1a0456
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-start-warning.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
+import { devWarn, isProduction } from '../../../internal/warn';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { DataGridColumnLayout } from '../types';
+
+const MESSAGE =
+  "<DataGrid> a column's `width`, `visible` and `pinned` only start the column layout. To change them after mount, change `columnLayout` (or remount the grid with a `key`).";
+
+interface Own {
+  width: number | undefined;
+  visible: boolean;
+  pinned: string | undefined;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Development only: warns once when, after a commit, the own `width`, `visible` or `pinned` of a
+ * column changed from what it said before and the layout shown does not already say the new value.
+ * A known column is laid out by the layout alone, so such a change would do nothing and say nothing.
+ * Compared by value per column id, so `columns` written in the JSX does not warn; a column that is
+ * new, or whose new value is the layout's own, does not either.
+ */
+export function useColumnStartWarning<TRow>(
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+  shown: DataGridColumnLayout,
+): void {
+  const before = useRef<Map<string, Own> | null>(null);
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (isProduction()) return;
+    const previous = before.current;
+    const now = new Map<string, Own>();
+    let ignored = false;
+    for (const { id, width, visible, pinned } of columns) {
+      now.set(id, { width, visible, pinned });
+      const was = previous?.get(id);
+      if (!was || ignored) continue;
+      const changed = {
+        width: was.width !== width && shown.widths[id] !== width,
+        visible: was.visible !== visible && !shown.hidden.includes(id) !== visible,
+        pinned: was.pinned !== pinned && shown.pinned[id] !== pinned,
+      };
+      ignored = changed.width || changed.visible || changed.pinned;
+    }
+    before.current = now;
+    if (ignored) devWarn(MESSAGE);
+  }, [columns, shown]);
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-kept.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-kept.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6e7d80e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-kept.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+import { useState } from 'react';
+
+/**
+ * The value of an earlier render for as long as `same` says the new one is the same: a value built
+ * again in every render (an object written in the JSX, a list a function makes) keeps its identity
+ * while it says the same, so what depends on its identity is not done again. The new value is kept
+ * the first time it is not the same, in this render and not after it, as the grid keeps its labels.
+ */
+export function useKept<T>(value: T, same: (kept: T, next: T) => boolean): T {
+  const [kept, keep] = useState(value);
+  if (kept === value || same(kept, value)) return kept;
+  keep(value);
+  return value;
+}
+
+/** Whether two lists hold the same items in the same order. */
+export function sameList<T>(a: readonly T[], b: readonly T[]): boolean {
+  return a.length === b.length && a.every((item, index) => Object.is(item, b[index]));
+}
+
+/** Whether two lists hold the same items, in any order. */
+export function sameMembers<T>(a: readonly T[], b: readonly T[]): boolean {
+  return (
+    a.length === b.length &&
+    a.every((item) => b.includes(item)) &&
+    b.every((item) => a.includes(item))
+  );
+}

### Task 3: cột ghim, vạch mép và bóng

Spec §1 (dòng "Cột ghim"), §3.6 ("Không bị header dính che", các câu cuối: trục ngang), §3.7 ("`table-layout: fixed` và `<colgroup>`": cột đệm; "Trước khi đo"; "Dính": bảng và gạch "Cột ghim"; "Nội dung trải cả hàng"), §3.9 (dòng "số đo"), §4.2 (`--flg-data-grid-pin-shadow`, `--flg-data-grid-pin-bg`), §4.3 G1 ("Cột ghim", "Dark"), §4.4 ("Không đo": vạch mép, bóng), §4.5 ("Ô ghim và tiêu đề dính"), §7 (lớp 2: cột ghim dính khi cuộn hai trục, chỉ đặc sau khi cuộn ngang, focus không bao giờ nằm dưới cột ghim), §10 (dòng "`sticky` lồng nhau"). Mockup G1: grid trên (cột chọn và Order ghim trái khi nghỉ: trong suốt, vạch mép bên phải Order) và crop 700px đã cuộn (ô ghim đặc, bóng, hover của DH-1030, nền và vạch 3px của DH-1028 qua ô ghim); story giao diện của chúng ở Task 8. Ô ghim trên khung `striped`/`minimal` ngoài mockup (chủ dự án chọn A).
- **Engine:** `pinOffsets`, `fillerIndex`, `pinPlaces` (phát hiện 9).
- **Vùng dính:** offset là custom property trên `<table>` do `GridTable` ghi; `minWidth` trước khi đo; thuộc tính `data-pinned`, `data-pin-edge` trên mọi loại ô qua `pin-attributes.ts`; cột chọn dòng ghim cùng vùng trái (phát hiện 9).
- **`usePinnedScroll`:** `data-scrolled-left/-right` và `--flg-data-grid-view-height` ghi thẳng lên khung, chỉ khi có cột ghim (phát hiện 9).
- **Giao diện G1:** ô đặc khi đã cuộn, nền dòng qua `::before` và `--flg-data-grid-wash`, vạch mép, bóng trên tiêu đề ô mép cao bằng phần thân đang hiện (OQ 2), token `--flg-data-grid-pin-shadow`, forced colors (phát hiện 9).
- **Cột đệm trước vùng phải** (OQ 3), `cellsOf` (phát hiện 9).
- **Scroll margin trên trục ngang** và `data-sticky-header` luôn có (phát hiện 9).
- **Khung `striped`/`minimal`:** `--flg-data-grid-pin-inset` (phương án A của chủ dự án, phát hiện 10).
- **Story** (file mới `DataGridColumns.stories.tsx`, `no-visual`, ba engine): `PinnedColumns`, `PinnedShadow`, `PinnedFocus`.
- **Docs:** mục "Pinned columns" của `DataGrid.mdx`, một câu về vùng, câu về cột đệm trong "Widths"; một câu về token trong `Theming.mdx`.
- Spec §3.6, §3.7, §3.9, §4.3 được sửa (phát hiện 22). Không lớp CSS mới.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-pinned-scroll.ts`, `parts/pin-attributes.ts`, `DataGrid.pinned.test.tsx`, `DataGridColumns.stories.tsx`
- Modify: `src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.tsx`, `engine/layout.ts`, `engine/layout.test.ts`, `grid-context.ts`, `grid-dom.ts`, `hooks/use-grid-keyboard.ts`, `parts/GridTable.tsx`, `parts/HeaderRow.tsx`, `parts/HeaderCell.tsx`, `parts/DataRow.tsx`, `parts/Cell.tsx`, `parts/SelectCells.tsx`, `parts/SkeletonRows.tsx`, `parts/FillerCell.tsx`, `DataGrid.renders.test.tsx`, `DataGrid.mdx`, `src/styles/components/data-grid.css`, `src/styles/preferences.css`, `src/styles/theme/values.ts`, `src/docs/Theming.mdx`, `scripts/lib/theme-css.test.ts`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-13-h2d-glass-ui-phase-6-design.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Nội bộ:
  - `engine/layout.ts`: `pinOffsets(widths: readonly number[], pins: readonly (DataGridPin | undefined)[])` → `(number | undefined)[]`; `fillerIndex(pins)` → `number` (chỗ của cột đệm: trước vùng phải, không có thì cuối); `PinPlace { side: DataGridPin; edge: boolean; style: { left: string } | { right: string } }`; `pinPlaces(pins)` → `(PinPlace | undefined)[]`.
  - `GridContext` thêm `pins: readonly (PinPlace | undefined)[]` (cột chọn dòng đầu) và `fillerAt: number`.
  - `grid-dom.ts`: `cellsOf(row: HTMLTableRowElement)` → các ô không kể ô đệm.
  - `hooks/use-pinned-scroll.ts`: `VIEW_HEIGHT_PROPERTY = '--flg-data-grid-view-height'`; `usePinnedScroll(frameRef, tableRef, enabled)`.
  - `parts/pin-attributes.ts`: `pinAttributes(place)` (`data-pinned`, `data-pin-edge`, `style`); `parts/FillerCell.tsx`: `placeFiller(cells, at, shown, head?)`; `Cell`, `SelectAllCell`, `SelectRowCell` nhận `pin`.
  - `GridTableProps` thêm `pins`, `fillerAt`.
- DOM: `[data-pinned="left" | "right"]` và `[data-pin-edge]` trên tiêu đề, ô dữ liệu, `th` tiêu đề dòng, ô skeleton và ô chọn của cột ghim; `[data-scrolled-left]`, `[data-scrolled-right]` trên khung; cột đệm (`<col>` và ô) ở `fillerAt`.
- CSS: custom property `--flg-data-grid-pin-<i>` (trên `style` của bảng), `--flg-data-grid-pinned-left`, `--flg-data-grid-pinned-right` (bảng, `0px`), `--flg-data-grid-view-height` và `--flg-data-grid-pin-inset` (khung), `--flg-data-grid-wash` (dòng); token `--flg-data-grid-pin-shadow` (light `color-mix(in srgb, var(--flg-text) 20%, transparent)`, dark `color-mix(in srgb, #000 62%, transparent)`). Không lớp mới.
- Story: `DataGridColumns.stories.tsx`, meta `title: 'Components/DataGrid/Columns'` (id `components-datagrid-columns--…`), `tags: ['unreleased']`; `PinnedColumns`, `PinnedShadow`, `PinnedFocus` (`no-visual`).
- Consumes: `applyLayout` (`pins`, `widths`), `useKept` (Task 2); `GridTable` (Task 1); `useColumnWidths` (px đã đo), `--flg-data-grid-pin-bg`, `scroll-margin-top` của Plan B.
- Task sau dùng: Task 4 đọc offset ghim trong độ rộng sống và đặt tay nắm dưới tiêu đề ghim; Task 5 dùng `pins` cho vùng của cú kéo; Task 6 dùng `pinColumn` qua menu; Task 8 chụp G1 với cột ghim. Plan D (ô ghim của hàng lọc), Plan E (cột dịch vụ của nhóm, `<tfoot>` ghim), Plan F (cột thao tác ghim phải).
