index 0000000..d90c9ab
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.pinned.test.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,551 @@
+import { act, createEvent, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { renderToString } from 'react-dom/server';
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { resetDevWarnings } from '../../internal/warn';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type { DataGridColumn, DataGridColumnLayout, DataGridProps } from './index';
+
+// The pinned columns (spec phase 6 §3.7, §4.3 G1): what each cell says about where it sticks, the
+// offsets the table writes, the attributes the frame gets from its scroll, and the filler column,
+// which goes before the right zone. What needs a layout engine to be true (a cell that stays where it
+// is, a shadow that is drawn) is proven in the stories (`DataGridColumns.stories.tsx`).
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  // jsdom has no layout, so every element would count as hidden to the code that looks for the
+  // controls of a cell.
+  HTMLElement.prototype.checkVisibility = () => true;
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'checkVisibility');
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  qty: number;
+  total: number;
+}
+
+const ORDERS: Order[] = [
+  { id: 'DH-1030', customer: 'Nguyễn Minh', qty: 4, total: 1250000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1029', customer: 'Trần Hải', qty: 1, total: 890000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1028', customer: 'Lê An', qty: 12, total: 15400000 },
+];
+
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+  { field: 'total', caption: 'Total', dataType: 'number', width: 120 },
+];
+
+const pinned = (parts: Record<string, 'left' | 'right'>): Partial<DataGridColumnLayout> => ({
+  pinned: parts,
+});
+
+function Orders(props: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>>) {
+  return (
+    <DataGrid
+      data={ORDERS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={false}
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+const grid = () => screen.getByRole('grid') as HTMLTableElement;
+const frame = () => grid().parentElement as HTMLElement;
+const headRow = () => grid().tHead!.rows[0]!;
+const bodyRows = () => Array.from(grid().tBodies[0]!.rows);
+const cellsIn = (row: HTMLTableRowElement) => Array.from(row.cells);
+/** The cells of a row as the words in them, with the filler column as `·`. */
+const kinds = (row: HTMLTableRowElement) =>
+  cellsIn(row).map((one) =>
+    one.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-filler') ? '·' : (one.textContent ?? ''),
+  );
+const prop = (name: string) => grid().style.getPropertyValue(name);
+
+const LEFT_AND_RIGHT = { id: 'left', customer: 'left', total: 'right' } as const;
+
+describe('what a cell of a pinned column says', () => {
+  it('has the side, the edge and the place it sticks to, in the title and in every row', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    const rows = [headRow(), ...bodyRows()];
+    expect(rows).toHaveLength(4);
+    for (const row of rows) {
+      const [order, customer, qty, , total] = cellsIn(row);
+      expect(order).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'left');
+      expect(order).not.toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+      expect(order).toHaveStyle({ left: 'var(--flg-data-grid-pin-0)' });
+      expect(customer).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'left');
+      expect(customer).toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+      expect(customer).toHaveStyle({ left: 'var(--flg-data-grid-pin-1)' });
+      expect(qty).not.toHaveAttribute('data-pinned');
+      expect(qty).not.toHaveAttribute('style');
+      expect(total).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'right');
+      expect(total).toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+      expect(total).toHaveStyle({ right: 'var(--flg-data-grid-pin-3)' });
+    }
+  });
+
+  it('is on the row header, which is a th of the body', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ id: 'left' })} />);
+    const header = bodyRows()[0]!.cells[0]!;
+    expect(header.tagName).toBe('TH');
+    expect(header).toHaveAttribute('scope', 'row');
+    expect(header).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'left');
+    expect(header).toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+  });
+
+  it('is on the cells of the skeleton rows', () => {
+    render(<Orders data={[]} loading defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    const skeleton = grid().querySelector<HTMLTableRowElement>('.flg-data-grid-skeleton-row')!;
+    expect(cellsIn(skeleton).map((one) => one.getAttribute('data-pinned'))).toEqual([
+      'left',
+      'left',
+      null,
+      null,
+      'right',
+    ]);
+    expect(cellsIn(skeleton)[1]).toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+    expect(cellsIn(skeleton)[1]).toHaveStyle({ left: 'var(--flg-data-grid-pin-1)' });
+  });
+
+  it('is on no cell of a grid with no pinned column, and no style is added', () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    expect(grid().querySelector('[data-pinned], [data-pin-edge]')).toBeNull();
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-0')).toBe('');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left')).toBe('');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-right')).toBe('');
+  });
+
+  it('follows a column that is pinned or unpinned after the grid is drawn', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout({})} />);
+    expect(grid().querySelector('[data-pinned]')).toBeNull();
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ qty: 'right' })} />);
+    // Qty goes to the right zone, after Total, and the filler column goes before it.
+    expect(headRow().cells[4]).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'right');
+    expect(bodyRows()[1]!.cells[4]).toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({})} />);
+    expect(grid().querySelector('[data-pinned]')).toBeNull();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('the column of boxes', () => {
+  it('is in the left zone when a data column is pinned to the left', () => {
+    render(<Orders selectionMode="multiple" defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ id: 'left' })} />);
+    for (const row of [headRow(), ...bodyRows()]) {
+      const [box, order, customer] = cellsIn(row);
+      expect(box).toHaveAttribute('data-service', 'select');
+      expect(box).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'left');
+      expect(box).not.toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+      expect(box).toHaveStyle({ left: 'var(--flg-data-grid-pin-0)' });
+      expect(order).toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+      expect(order).toHaveStyle({ left: 'var(--flg-data-grid-pin-1)' });
+      expect(customer).not.toHaveAttribute('data-pinned');
+    }
+    // The box is 40px wide and Order 104px: the zone is 144px, and Order sticks after the box.
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-1')).toContain('40px');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left')).toBe('144px');
+  });
+
+  it('is not pinned when only a column to the right is, nor when none is', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(
+      <Orders selectionMode="multiple" defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ total: 'right' })} />,
+    );
+    expect(headRow().cells[0]).not.toHaveAttribute('data-pinned');
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('[data-pinned="left"]')).toHaveLength(0);
+    rerender(<Orders selectionMode="multiple" columnLayout={layout({})} />);
+    expect(grid().querySelector('[data-pinned]')).toBeNull();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('where the table says the columns stick', () => {
+  it('writes the offset of each pinned column and the width of each zone', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    // The inset is taken back in the property, so a cell only reads it (6px in `striped`).
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-0')).toBe('calc(0px - var(--flg-data-grid-pin-inset))');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-1')).toBe('calc(104px - var(--flg-data-grid-pin-inset))');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-3')).toBe('calc(0px - var(--flg-data-grid-pin-inset))');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-2')).toBe('');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left')).toBe('304px');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-right')).toBe('120px');
+  });
+
+  const FLEXIBLE: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+    { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, minWidth: 90 },
+    { ...COLUMNS[1]! },
+    { ...COLUMNS[2]! },
+    { ...COLUMNS[3]! },
+  ];
+
+  it('counts the least width of a flexible pinned column before the frame is measured', () => {
+    render(
+      <Orders columns={FLEXIBLE} defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ id: 'left', customer: 'left' })} />,
+    );
+    // The table has no room to share out yet, so Order rests at its least, and Customer sticks no
+    // further right than where it rests.
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-1')).toBe('calc(90px - var(--flg-data-grid-pin-inset))');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left')).toBe('290px');
+  });
+
+  it('counts the width it was given once the frame is measured', () => {
+    vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'clientWidth', 'get').mockImplementation(function (
+      this: HTMLElement,
+    ) {
+      return this.classList.contains('flg-table-frame') ? 1000 : 0;
+    });
+    render(
+      <Orders columns={FLEXIBLE} defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ id: 'left', customer: 'left' })} />,
+    );
+    // 1000 less the 400 of the other three is the 600 that Order takes.
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('col')[0]).toHaveStyle({ width: '600px' });
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-1')).toBe('calc(600px - var(--flg-data-grid-pin-inset))');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left')).toBe('800px');
+  });
+
+  it('is written by the table alone: a width that changes draws no cell', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ id: 'left', customer: 'left' })} />);
+    const before = bodyRows()[0]!.cells[1]!;
+    rerender(
+      <Orders
+        columnLayout={layout({ id: 'left', customer: 'left' }, { id: 150, customer: 200 })}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pin-1')).toBe('calc(150px - var(--flg-data-grid-pin-inset))');
+    expect(prop('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left')).toBe('350px');
+    expect(bodyRows()[0]!.cells[1]).toBe(before);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('the scroll of a frame with a pinned column', () => {
+  // jsdom has no layout: the frame says what the test tells it to.
+  function scrollBox(box: {
+    scrollLeft?: number;
+    clientWidth?: number;
+    scrollWidth?: number;
+    scrollTop?: number;
+    clientHeight?: number;
+    offsetTop?: number;
+    offsetHeight?: number;
+  }) {
+    const element = frame();
+    const table = grid();
+    const define = (target: HTMLElement, name: string, value: number | undefined) => {
+      if (value === undefined) return;
+      Object.defineProperty(target, name, { configurable: true, value });
+    };
+    define(element, 'scrollLeft', box.scrollLeft);
+    define(element, 'clientWidth', box.clientWidth);
+    define(element, 'scrollWidth', box.scrollWidth);
+    define(element, 'scrollTop', box.scrollTop);
+    define(element, 'clientHeight', box.clientHeight);
+    define(table, 'offsetTop', box.offsetTop);
+    define(table, 'offsetHeight', box.offsetHeight);
+  }
+  const scroll = () => act(() => void fireEvent.scroll(frame()));
+  const scrolledLeft = () => frame().hasAttribute('data-scrolled-left');
+  const scrolledRight = () => frame().hasAttribute('data-scrolled-right');
+
+  it('says which sides are scrolled, from what the frame has beyond what it shows', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 0, clientWidth: 500, scrollWidth: 900 });
+    scroll();
+    // At rest the columns to the right are under the right zone, the ones to the left are not.
+    expect(scrolledLeft()).toBe(false);
+    expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(true);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 120 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(scrolledLeft()).toBe(true);
+    expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(true);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 400 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(scrolledLeft()).toBe(true);
+    expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(false);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 399.5 });
+    scroll();
+    // A pixel short of the end is the end: a fraction is no scroll.
+    expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(false);
+  });
+
+  it('says nothing for a frame that holds all its columns', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 0, clientWidth: 900, scrollWidth: 900 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(scrolledLeft()).toBe(false);
+    expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(false);
+    expect(frame().style.getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-view-height')).toBe('');
+  });
+
+  it('writes an attribute only when its value changes', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 0, clientWidth: 500, scrollWidth: 900 });
+    scroll();
+    const set = vi.spyOn(frame(), 'setAttribute');
+    const remove = vi.spyOn(frame(), 'removeAttribute');
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 10 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(set).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 20 });
+    scroll();
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 30 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(set).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    expect(remove).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('gives the shadow the height of what the body shows, never more than the last row', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    const view = () => frame().style.getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-view-height');
+    // A table of 120px in a frame of 300px: the shadow ends with the last row.
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 50, clientWidth: 500, scrollWidth: 900, clientHeight: 300 });
+    scrollBox({ scrollTop: 0, offsetTop: 0, offsetHeight: 120 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(view()).toBe('120px');
+    // A table taller than the frame: the frame.
+    scrollBox({ offsetHeight: 500 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(view()).toBe('300px');
+    // Scrolled so that the end of the table is in sight: what shows of it.
+    scrollBox({ scrollTop: 400 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(view()).toBe('100px');
+    // A `striped` frame has padding: the table starts below the top, and the heading with it.
+    scrollBox({ scrollTop: 0, offsetTop: 6, offsetHeight: 120 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(view()).toBe('120px');
+  });
+
+  it('takes the height off when nothing is scrolled any more', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 50, clientWidth: 500, scrollWidth: 900, clientHeight: 300 });
+    scrollBox({ scrollTop: 0, offsetTop: 0, offsetHeight: 120 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(frame().style.getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-view-height')).toBe('120px');
+    scrollBox({ scrollWidth: 500, scrollLeft: 0 });
+    scroll();
+    expect(frame().style.getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-view-height')).toBe('');
+  });
+
+  it('listens to the frame once, passively, and only while a column is pinned', () => {
+    const add = vi.spyOn(EventTarget.prototype, 'addEventListener');
+    const remove = vi.spyOn(EventTarget.prototype, 'removeEventListener');
+    const onFrame = (spy: typeof add) =>
+      spy.mock.calls.filter(
+        ([type], index) => type === 'scroll' && spy.mock.contexts[index] === frame(),
+      );
+    const { rerender, unmount } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout({})} />);
+    expect(onFrame(add)).toHaveLength(0);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ qty: 'right' })} />);
+    expect(onFrame(add)).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(onFrame(add)[0]![2]).toEqual({ passive: true });
+    // More pins, and the same listener.
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ qty: 'right', id: 'left' })} />);
+    expect(onFrame(add)).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(onFrame(remove)).toHaveLength(0);
+    // The last pin goes: the listener and what it wrote go.
+    scrollFrameBy(500, 900);
+    scroll();
+    expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(true);
+    rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({})} />);
+    expect(onFrame(remove)).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(scrolledLeft()).toBe(false);
+    expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(false);
+    unmount();
+  });
+
+  function scrollFrameBy(clientWidth: number, scrollWidth: number) {
+    scrollBox({ scrollLeft: 0, clientWidth, scrollWidth });
+  }
+
+  it('lets go of the listener and of the observer when the grid goes', () => {
+    const remove = vi.spyOn(EventTarget.prototype, 'removeEventListener');
+    const disconnect = vi.fn();
+    class Observer {
+      observe = vi.fn();
+      unobserve = vi.fn();
+      disconnect = disconnect;
+    }
+    vi.stubGlobal('ResizeObserver', Observer);
+    try {
+      const { unmount } = render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned(LEFT_AND_RIGHT)} />);
+      const element = frame();
+      scrollFrameBy(500, 900);
+      scroll();
+      expect(scrolledRight()).toBe(true);
+      unmount();
+      expect(
+        remove.mock.calls.filter(
+          ([type], index) => type === 'scroll' && remove.mock.contexts[index] === element,
+        ),
+      ).toHaveLength(1);
+      expect(disconnect).toHaveBeenCalled();
+      expect(element.hasAttribute('data-scrolled-right')).toBe(false);
+    } finally {
+      vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+    }
+  });
+
+  it('watches the frame and the table, and only while a column is pinned', () => {
+    const observed: Element[] = [];
+    class Observer {
+      constructor(public callback: () => void) {}
+      observe = (element: Element) => void observed.push(element);
+      unobserve = vi.fn();
+      disconnect = vi.fn();
+    }
+    vi.stubGlobal('ResizeObserver', Observer);
+    try {
+      const { rerender } = render(<Orders columnLayout={layout({})} />);
+      // Every column has a width, so the grid watches its frame for the filler column.
+      const before = observed.length;
+      rerender(<Orders columnLayout={layout({ qty: 'right' })} />);
+      expect(observed.slice(before)).toEqual([frame(), grid()]);
+    } finally {
+      vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+    }
+  });
+});
+
+/** A layout of the four columns with the pins given, and the widths of the columns. */
+function layout(
+  pins: Record<string, 'left' | 'right'>,
+  widths: Record<string, number> = { id: 104, customer: 200, qty: 80, total: 120 },
+): DataGridColumnLayout {
+  return { order: ['id', 'customer', 'qty', 'total'], widths, hidden: [], pinned: pins };
+}
+
+describe('the filler column', () => {
+  it('is at the end of the row when no column is pinned to the right', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ id: 'left' })} />);
+    expect(kinds(headRow())).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total', '·']);
+    for (const row of bodyRows()) {
+      expect(cellsIn(row)).toHaveLength(5);
+      expect(kinds(row).indexOf('·')).toBe(4);
+    }
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('col')[4]).not.toHaveAttribute('style');
+  });
+
+  it('is before the right zone in the colgroup, the title, the rows and the skeleton rows', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(
+      <Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ qty: 'right', total: 'right' })} />,
+    );
+    const cols = Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll('col'));
+    expect(cols).toHaveLength(5);
+    // The columns in order: Order, Customer, the filler (no width), then the zone, Qty and Total.
+    expect(cols.map((col) => col.style.width)).toEqual(['104px', '200px', '', '80px', '120px']);
+    expect(kinds(headRow())).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', '·', 'Qty', 'Total']);
+    for (const row of bodyRows()) {
+      expect(kinds(row).indexOf('·')).toBe(2);
+      expect(cellsIn(row)).toHaveLength(5);
+    }
+    rerender(
+      <Orders data={[]} loading defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ qty: 'right', total: 'right' })} />,
+    );
+    for (const row of grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLTableRowElement>('.flg-data-grid-skeleton-row')) {
+      expect(kinds(row).indexOf('·')).toBe(2);
+    }
+  });
+
+  it('is before the right zone when the zone is the whole row but one', () => {
+    render(
+      <Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ customer: 'right', qty: 'right', total: 'right' })} />,
+    );
+    expect(kinds(headRow())).toEqual(['Order', '·', 'Customer', 'Qty', 'Total']);
+  });
+
+  it('is in no keyboard path: End, Left and Right go across it', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ qty: 'right', total: 'right' })} />);
+    const row = () => bodyRows()[0]!;
+    const press = (element: HTMLElement, key: string) => {
+      const event = createEvent.keyDown(element, { key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true });
+      act(() => void fireEvent(element, event));
+    };
+    // Order, Customer, filler, Qty, Total.
+    act(() => row().cells[1]!.focus());
+    press(row().cells[1]!, 'ArrowRight');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(row().cells[3]);
+    press(row().cells[3]!, 'ArrowLeft');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(row().cells[1]);
+    press(row().cells[1]!, 'End');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(row().cells[4]);
+    press(row().cells[4]!, 'Home');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(row().cells[0]);
+    // The cell of the right zone is the third column to the keyboard, not the fourth.
+    act(() => row().cells[4]!.focus());
+    press(row().cells[4]!, 'ArrowDown');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(bodyRows()[1]!.cells[4]);
+    press(bodyRows()[1]!.cells[4]!, 'ArrowUp');
+    press(row().cells[4]!, 'ArrowUp');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(headRow().cells[4]);
+    press(headRow().cells[4]!, 'ArrowLeft');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(headRow().cells[3]);
+    press(headRow().cells[3]!, 'ArrowLeft');
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(headRow().cells[1]);
+  });
+
+  it('is no place of the keyboard: the active cell keeps its place across a press on it', () => {
+    render(<Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ qty: 'right', total: 'right' })} />);
+    const row = bodyRows()[1]!;
+    act(() => row.cells[3]!.focus());
+    const filler = row.cells[2]!;
+    expect(filler).toHaveClass('flg-data-grid-filler');
+    const event = createEvent.mouseDown(filler, { bubbles: true, cancelable: true });
+    act(() => void fireEvent(filler, event));
+    expect(event.defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(row.cells[3]);
+    expect(Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll('[tabindex="0"]'))).toEqual([row.cells[3]]);
+  });
+
+  it('does not activate a row from a double press on it', () => {
+    const onRowActivate = vi.fn();
+    render(
+      <Orders
+        onRowActivate={onRowActivate}
+        defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ qty: 'right', total: 'right' })}
+      />,
+    );
+    act(() => void fireEvent.doubleClick(bodyRows()[0]!.cells[2]!));
+    expect(onRowActivate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    act(() => void fireEvent.doubleClick(bodyRows()[0]!.cells[4]!));
+    expect(onRowActivate).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('the HTML of the server', () => {
+  const headOf = (html: string) => {
+    const holder = document.createElement('div');
+    holder.innerHTML = html;
+    return Array.from(holder.querySelector('thead tr')!.children, (one) =>
+      one.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-filler') ? '·' : one.textContent,
+    );
+  };
+
+  it('has the offsets from the least widths of the columns that have none', () => {
+    const html = renderToString(
+      <Orders
+        columns={[{ ...COLUMNS[0]!, width: undefined, minWidth: 90 }, ...COLUMNS.slice(1)]}
+        defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ id: 'left', total: 'right' })}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(html).toContain('data-pinned="left"');
+    expect(html).toContain('data-pinned="right"');
+    // Nothing is measured on the server: a flexible column counts its least width.
+    expect(html).toContain('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left:90px');
+    expect(html).toContain('--flg-data-grid-pinned-right:120px');
+    // The scroll is a client matter: the server draws the grid at rest.
+    expect(html).not.toContain('data-scrolled');
+  });
+
+  it('has the filler column before the right zone', () => {
+    const html = renderToString(
+      <Orders defaultColumnLayout={pinned({ id: 'left', total: 'right' })} />,
+    );
+    expect(headOf(html)).toEqual(['Order', 'Customer', 'Qty', '·', 'Total']);
+  });
+});
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.renders.test.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.renders.test.tsx
index 4e0f27a..5e9ee88 100644
--- a/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.renders.test.tsx
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.renders.test.tsx
@@ -223,3 +223,63 @@ describe('the layout of the columns', () => {
     expect(renders.cell).toBe(5 * 3);
   });
 });
+
+// Pinned columns (phase 6 Plan C): the scroll of the frame is written to its attributes directly, so
+// it draws nothing, and a pin is a change of what every cell says, which draws the rows once.
+describe('a grid with a pinned column', () => {
+  const PINNED = (pinned: DataGridColumnLayout['pinned']): DataGridColumnLayout => ({
+    order: ['id', 'customer', 'qty'],
+    widths: { id: 104, customer: 200, qty: 80 },
+    hidden: [],
+    pinned,
+  });
+  const small = (columnLayout: DataGridColumnLayout) => (
+    <DataGrid
+      data={ORDERS.slice(0, 5)}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={false}
+      columnLayout={columnLayout}
+    />
+  );
+  const reset = () => {
+    renders.cell = 0;
+    renders.headerCell = 0;
+    renders.toolbar = 0;
+    renders.body = 0;
+  };
+
+  it('draws no toolbar, title, row or body for a scroll of its frame', () => {
+    render(small(PINNED({ id: 'left', qty: 'right' })));
+    const frame = grid().parentElement!;
+    reset();
+    for (const left of [0, 30, 60, 100]) {
+      Object.defineProperty(frame, 'scrollLeft', { configurable: true, value: left });
+      Object.defineProperty(frame, 'clientWidth', { configurable: true, value: 200 });
+      Object.defineProperty(frame, 'scrollWidth', { configurable: true, value: 400 });
+      act(() => void fireEvent.scroll(frame));
+    }
+    // It did something: the frame says it is scrolled from its left end.
+    expect(frame).toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-left');
+    expect(frame).toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-right');
+    expect(renders.toolbar).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.body).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it('draws the rows once for a column that is pinned, and no more for its width', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(small(PINNED({})));
+    reset();
+    rerender(small(PINNED({ id: 'left' })));
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(3);
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(5 * 3);
+    reset();
+    rerender(small({ ...PINNED({ id: 'left' }), widths: { id: 150, customer: 200, qty: 80 } }));
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(0);
+    expect(grid().style.getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-pin-0')).toContain('0px');
+    expect(grid().style.getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left')).toBe('150px');
+  });
+});
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGridColumns.stories.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGridColumns.stories.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..856bafa
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGridColumns.stories.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,418 @@
+import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
+import { useRef } from 'react';
+import { expect, waitFor } from 'storybook/test';
+import { SALES, SALE_COLUMNS } from '../../../.storybook/data-grid-orders';
+import type { Sale } from '../../../.storybook/data-grid-orders';
+import { realUserEvent } from '../../../.storybook/real-input';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type { DataGridHandle, DataGridProps } from './index';
+
+const meta = {
+  title: 'Components/DataGrid/Columns',
+  component: DataGrid,
+  // Built but not released until the grid is exported (spec phase 6 §2): hidden from the sidebar of
+  // the built docs, still run by the story tests and shot by the visual harness.
+  tags: ['unreleased'],
+  args: { data: SALES, rowKey: 'id', columns: SALE_COLUMNS, 'aria-label': 'Orders' },
+  parameters: {
+    a11y: {
+      config: {
+        rules: [{ id: 'region', enabled: false }],
+      },
+    },
+  },
+} satisfies Meta<DataGridProps<Sale>>;
+
+export default meta;
+type Story = StoryObj<DataGridProps<Sale>>;
+
+/** Two animation frames: a scroll event is delivered, and what listens to it has written, by then. */
+const frames = async () => {
+  await new Promise((resolve) => requestAnimationFrame(resolve));
+  await new Promise((resolve) => requestAnimationFrame(resolve));
+};
+
+const frameOf = (grid: HTMLElement) =>
+  grid.closest('.flg-data-grid')!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-frame')!;
+const tableOf = (grid: HTMLElement) => grid.querySelector<HTMLTableElement>('table[role="grid"]')!;
+
+/** The sides of a box as distances from the inside of the frame (its border is not part of what scrolls). */
+function boxIn(frame: HTMLElement, element: Element) {
+  const outer = frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+  const box = element.getBoundingClientRect();
+  const left = outer.left + frame.clientLeft;
+  const top = outer.top + frame.clientTop;
+  return {
+    left: box.left - left,
+    right: box.right - left,
+    top: box.top - top,
+    bottom: box.bottom - top,
+  };
+}
+
+/** The colour that the grid says is solid, as the browser computes it. */
+const solid = (frame: HTMLElement) => {
+  const probe = document.createElement('div');
+  probe.style.backgroundColor = 'var(--flg-data-grid-pin-bg)';
+  frame.append(probe);
+  const colour = getComputedStyle(probe).backgroundColor;
+  probe.remove();
+  return colour;
+};
+
+/** Whether the element at the middle of `cell` is the cell, or something in it. */
+const hitsItself = (cell: Element) => {
+  const box = cell.getBoundingClientRect();
+  const hit = document.elementFromPoint(box.left + box.width / 2, box.top + box.height / 2);
+  return hit !== null && (hit === cell || cell.contains(hit));
+};
+
+/** The grids of the pinned stories: the frame is narrower than the columns, and has a height. */
+const PinnedGrid = ({
+  variant,
+  label,
+  rows = 30,
+  height = 260,
+}: {
+  variant: 'lined' | 'striped' | 'minimal';
+  label: string;
+  rows?: number;
+  height?: number;
+}) => (
+  <div style={{ width: 640, marginBottom: 12 }}>
+    <DataGrid
+      aria-label={label}
+      data-testid={label}
+      data={SALES.slice(0, rows)}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={SALE_COLUMNS}
+      variant={variant}
+      height={height}
+      paging={false}
+      selectionMode="multiple"
+      defaultColumnLayout={{ pinned: { id: 'left', total: 'right' } }}
+    />
+  </div>
+);
+
+/**
+ * Pinned columns in each look: the box column and Order stick to the left and Total to the right while
+ * the frame scrolls both ways. Layout, sticking and what is under the pointer are facts of a layout
+ * engine, so they are measured in each engine and not read from the stylesheet: a pinned cell stays
+ * where it is, is the one under the pointer (not the cell that scrolled beneath), is solid only on a side
+ * that has been scrolled, and the titles stay over it. The 6px of padding a `striped` or `minimal`
+ * frame has shows no strip of scrolled cells beside a zone.
+ */
+export const PinnedColumns: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  render: () => (
+    <>
+      <PinnedGrid variant="lined" label="Lined" />
+      <PinnedGrid variant="striped" label="Striped" />
+      <PinnedGrid variant="minimal" label="Minimal" />
+    </>
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    for (const label of ['Lined', 'Striped', 'Minimal']) {
+      const grid = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-testid="${label}"]`)!;
+      const wrapper = grid.closest<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+      wrapper.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' });
+      const frame = frameOf(wrapper);
+      const table = tableOf(wrapper);
+      await waitFor(() => expect(frame.clientHeight).toBeGreaterThan(100));
+      const inset = Number.parseFloat(
+        getComputedStyle(frame).getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-pin-inset'),
+      );
+      await expect(inset).toBe(label === 'Lined' ? 0 : 6);
+      // The table is wider than the frame, so there is something to scroll both ways.
+      await expect(frame.scrollWidth).toBeGreaterThan(frame.clientWidth + 400);
+      await expect(frame.scrollHeight).toBeGreaterThan(frame.clientHeight + 200);
+
+      const heading = table.tHead!.rows[0]!;
+      // A row with no stripe, so a cell of it has no background of its own at rest.
+      const row = table.tBodies[0]!.rows[1]!;
+      // The cells: the box column, Order and Customer... and Total, with the filler before the right zone
+      // (there is none: the columns do not fit, so the table is as wide as they are).
+      const cells = (from: HTMLTableRowElement) => Array.from(from.cells);
+      const box = cells(row)[0]!;
+      const order = cells(row)[1]!;
+      const customer = cells(row)[2]!;
+      const total = cells(row).at(-1)!;
+      await expect(box).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'left');
+      await expect(order).toHaveAttribute('data-pin-edge');
+      await expect(total).toHaveAttribute('data-pinned', 'right');
+      const pinnedTitles = cells(heading).filter((cell) => cell.hasAttribute('data-pinned'));
+      await expect(pinnedTitles).toHaveLength(3);
+
+      // At rest: nothing is scrolled to the left, the right zone has the columns under it.
+      frame.scrollLeft = 0;
+      frame.scrollTop = 0;
+      await frames();
+      const rest = {
+        box: boxIn(frame, box),
+        order: boxIn(frame, order),
+        total: boxIn(frame, total),
+      };
+      await expect(frame).not.toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-left');
+      await expect(frame).toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-right');
+      await expect(getComputedStyle(box).backgroundColor).toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
+      await expect(getComputedStyle(order).backgroundColor).toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
+      await expect(getComputedStyle(total).backgroundColor).toBe(solid(frame));
+      // The right zone ends at the edge of what the frame shows, whatever the padding.
+      await expect(rest.total.right).toBeCloseTo(frame.clientWidth, 0);
+
+      // Scrolled sideways and down: each pinned cell is where it was (the left zone has moved the
+      // inset of a padded frame, which the offsets take back), and is the one under the pointer.
+      for (const [left, top] of [
+        [200, 0],
+        [200, 90],
+        [500, 90],
+      ] as const) {
+        frame.scrollLeft = left;
+        frame.scrollTop = top;
+        await waitFor(() => expect(frame).toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-left'));
+        await frames();
+        await expect(Math.abs(frame.scrollLeft - left)).toBeLessThan(1);
+        const at = (cell: HTMLElement) => boxIn(frame, cell);
+        await expect(at(box).left).toBeCloseTo(rest.box.left - inset, 0);
+        await expect(at(order).left).toBeCloseTo(rest.order.left - inset, 0);
+        await expect(at(total).right).toBeCloseTo(rest.total.right, 0);
+        // The cell of the middle has gone under the zone.
+        await expect(at(customer).left).toBeLessThan(at(order).right);
+        // A pinned cell is the one under the pointer, in the part of the frame it is in view.
+        for (const cell of [box, order, total]) {
+          const where = at(cell);
+          if (where.top >= 0 && where.bottom <= frame.clientHeight) {
+            await expect(hitsItself(cell)).toBe(true);
+          }
+        }
+        // Solid, and the same colour as the heading's solid, on the side that is scrolled.
+        await expect(getComputedStyle(box).backgroundColor).toBe(solid(frame));
+        await expect(getComputedStyle(order).backgroundColor).toBe(solid(frame));
+        await expect(getComputedStyle(total).backgroundColor).toBe(solid(frame));
+        // The titles stay where they were, and over the pinned cells that scrolled up under them.
+        // They are in the row of the other titles, which stick to the top of the frame under the heading.
+        const plain = boxIn(frame, cells(heading)[3]!);
+        for (const title of pinnedTitles) {
+          await expect(boxIn(frame, title).top).toBeCloseTo(plain.top, 0);
+          await expect(hitsItself(title)).toBe(true);
+        }
+        // A heading that has been scrolled past sticks at the top of what the frame shows.
+        if (top > 0) await expect(plain.top).toBeLessThan(3);
+        const titleBox = boxIn(frame, pinnedTitles[1]!);
+        await expect(titleBox.left).toBeCloseTo(rest.order.left - inset, 0);
+        // No strip of the cells that scrolled beside a zone: at the left edge of what the frame shows
+        // and at the right edge, below the heading, the pinned cell is the one hit.
+        const outer = frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+        const midY = outer.top + frame.clientTop + frame.clientHeight - 20;
+        const hitLeft = document.elementFromPoint(outer.left + frame.clientLeft + 1, midY);
+        await expect(hitLeft?.closest('[data-pinned="left"]')).not.toBeNull();
+        const hitRight = document.elementFromPoint(
+          outer.left + frame.clientLeft + frame.clientWidth - 2,
+          midY,
+        );
+        await expect(hitRight?.closest('[data-pinned="right"]')).not.toBeNull();
+      }
+
+      // At the right end the right zone has nothing under it any more, and is transparent again.
+      frame.scrollLeft = frame.scrollWidth;
+      await waitFor(() => expect(frame).not.toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-right'));
+      await expect(getComputedStyle(total).backgroundColor).toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
+      await expect(getComputedStyle(order).backgroundColor).toBe(solid(frame));
+      await expect(frame).toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-left');
+    }
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * The shadow beside the edge of a zone: it is as tall as the part of the table the frame shows, and
+ * never reaches below the last row into the empty part of a frame with a height. It is drawn only on a
+ * side that is scrolled, and takes no press.
+ */
+export const PinnedShadow: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  render: () => (
+    <>
+      <PinnedGrid variant="lined" label="Tall" />
+      <PinnedGrid variant="lined" label="Short" rows={3} height={360} />
+    </>
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const shadow = (frame: HTMLElement, side: 'left' | 'right') => {
+      const title = frame.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
+        `thead [data-pinned="${side}"][data-pin-edge]`,
+      )!;
+      return { title, style: getComputedStyle(title, '::after') };
+    };
+    for (const label of ['Tall', 'Short']) {
+      const wrapper = canvasElement
+        .querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-testid="${label}"]`)!
+        .closest<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+      wrapper.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' });
+      const frame = frameOf(wrapper);
+      const table = tableOf(wrapper);
+      await waitFor(() => expect(frame.clientHeight).toBeGreaterThan(100));
+      frame.scrollLeft = 0;
+      await frames();
+      // At rest only the right side is scrolled: no shadow on the left.
+      await expect(shadow(frame, 'left').style.content).toBe('none');
+      await expect(shadow(frame, 'right').style.content).not.toBe('none');
+      frame.scrollLeft = 200;
+      await waitFor(() => expect(frame).toHaveAttribute('data-scrolled-left'));
+      await frames();
+      const left = shadow(frame, 'left');
+      await expect(left.style.content).not.toBe('none');
+      await expect(left.style.width).toBe('14px');
+      await expect(left.style.pointerEvents).toBe('none');
+      await expect(left.style.backgroundImage).toContain('linear-gradient');
+      const height = Number.parseFloat(left.style.height);
+      // What the frame shows of the table: from the top of the heading to the end of the last row or the
+      // bottom of the frame.
+      const shown = Math.min(frame.clientHeight, table.offsetHeight);
+      await expect(height).toBeCloseTo(shown, 0);
+      await expect(height).toBeLessThanOrEqual(table.offsetHeight + 0.5);
+      // It is drawn to the right of the edge cell, and in that much space: the rows it is over are
+      // the ones of the middle.
+      const edge = boxIn(frame, left.title);
+      await expect(edge.right).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    }
+    // The short grid is the one that shows the difference: its frame is taller than its table.
+    const short = frameOf(
+      canvasElement
+        .querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-testid="Short"]')!
+        .closest<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!,
+    );
+    await expect(short.clientHeight).toBeGreaterThan(tableOf(short).offsetHeight + 40);
+  },
+};
+
+/** A grid with the buttons around it for the focus to leave and come back by, and its handle. */
+function FocusGrid({ onHandle }: { onHandle: (handle: DataGridHandle | null) => void }) {
+  const ref = useRef<DataGridHandle | null>(null);
+  return (
+    <div style={{ width: 640 }}>
+      <button type="button">Before</button>
+      <DataGrid
+        ref={(handle) => {
+          ref.current = handle;
+          onHandle(handle);
+        }}
+        aria-label="Focus"
+        data-testid="Focus"
+        data={SALES.slice(0, 30)}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={SALE_COLUMNS}
+        height={260}
+        paging={false}
+        defaultColumnLayout={{ pinned: { id: 'left', total: 'right' } }}
+      />
+      <button type="button">After</button>
+    </div>
+  );
+}
+
+let handle: DataGridHandle | null = null;
+
+/**
+ * What takes the focus never scrolls the frame by a pinned column: moving by the keys onto a pinned
+ * cell, Tab out of the grid and back in, and the handle's `focus()` leave `scrollLeft` where it was
+ * (the browser's own focus scroll takes the sticky zone for a part that hides the cell in WebKit and
+ * Chromium); moving onto a cell of the middle stops it clear of both zones.
+ */
+export const PinnedFocus: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  render: () => <FocusGrid onHandle={(next) => void (handle = next)} />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const wrapper = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    wrapper.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' });
+    const frame = frameOf(wrapper);
+    const table = tableOf(wrapper);
+    await waitFor(() => expect(frame.clientHeight).toBeGreaterThan(100));
+    const cell = (row: number, column: number) => table.tBodies[0]!.rows[row]!.cells[column]!;
+    const zones = () => ({
+      left: Number.parseFloat(
+        getComputedStyle(table).getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-pinned-left'),
+      ),
+      right: Number.parseFloat(
+        getComputedStyle(table).getPropertyValue('--flg-data-grid-pinned-right'),
+      ),
+    });
+    await expect(zones()).toEqual({ left: 104, right: 180 });
+    const clearOfZones = async (element: HTMLElement) => {
+      const where = boxIn(frame, element);
+      await expect(where.left).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(zones().left - 0.5);
+      await expect(where.right).toBeLessThanOrEqual(frame.clientWidth - zones().right + 0.5);
+    };
+    // The cells: Order (pinned), Customer, Assignee, Order date, Status, Channel, Qty, Total (pinned).
+    // Start on Customer in the middle of the frame, scrolled so that it is at the edge of the zone.
+    frame.scrollLeft = 120;
+    await frames();
+    cell(2, 1).focus({ preventScroll: true });
+    await expect(cell(2, 1)).toHaveFocus();
+    const kept = frame.scrollLeft;
+
+    // Left onto Order: pinned, so nothing scrolls.
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
+    await expect(cell(2, 0)).toHaveFocus();
+    await frames();
+    await expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBe(kept);
+    await expect(frame.scrollTop).toBe(0);
+    // Right onto Customer: it is under the zone, so the frame scrolls it clear, and not more.
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
+    await expect(cell(2, 1)).toHaveFocus();
+    await frames();
+    await clearOfZones(cell(2, 1));
+    await expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBeLessThanOrEqual(kept);
+    // Across to the right zone and back: onto Total nothing scrolls, onto Qty it stops clear of it.
+    await real.keyboard('{End}');
+    await expect(cell(2, 7)).toHaveFocus();
+    await frames();
+    const atTotal = frame.scrollLeft;
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
+    await expect(cell(2, 6)).toHaveFocus();
+    await frames();
+    await clearOfZones(cell(2, 6));
+    const atQty = frame.scrollLeft;
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
+    await expect(cell(2, 7)).toHaveFocus();
+    await frames();
+    await expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBe(atQty);
+    await expect(atTotal).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
+
+    // The title of a pinned column, from its cell: no scroll either.
+    await real.keyboard('{Home}');
+    await expect(cell(2, 0)).toHaveFocus();
+    await frames();
+    const withOrder = frame.scrollLeft;
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowUp}{ArrowUp}{ArrowUp}');
+    await frames();
+    await expect(table.tHead!.rows[0]!.cells[0]).toHaveFocus();
+    await expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBe(withOrder);
+    await expect(frame.scrollTop).toBe(0);
+
+    // Tab out of the grid and back in: the focus returns to the pinned cell, and the frame stays put.
+    frame.scrollLeft = 300;
+    await frames();
+    const scrolled = frame.scrollLeft;
+    await real.tab();
+    await expect(document.activeElement?.textContent).toBe('After');
+    await real.tab({ shift: true });
+    await expect(table.tHead!.rows[0]!.cells[0]).toHaveFocus();
+    await frames();
+    await expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBe(scrolled);
+    await expect(frame.scrollTop).toBe(0);
+
+    // The handle's `focus()`, to a pinned cell, and with the frame scrolled both ways.
+    frame.scrollTop = 120;
+    await frames();
+    const down = frame.scrollTop;
+    (document.activeElement as HTMLElement).blur();
+    handle!.focus();
+    await frames();
+    await expect(document.activeElement).toBe(table.tHead!.rows[0]!.cells[0]);
+    await expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBe(scrolled);
+    await expect(frame.scrollTop).toBe(down);
+  },
+};

Di chuyển bằng phím gọi `focus({ preventScroll: true })` rồi `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })` của **ô** (cả khi control trong ô giữ focus), cái tôn trọng `scroll-margin` của ô và `scroll-padding` của khung. Cuộn ảo: cuộn tới độ lệch tính được, render, rồi focus. **Đi trên tiêu đề không cuộn khung theo chiều dọc** (phát hiện khi review PR #42): tiêu đề dính ở đầu khung, trong `scroll-padding-top` của `Table`, và Chromium với WebKit coi phần đệm đó là phần che nó, nên đo bằng story `TitlesKeepScroll` (khung cuộn ở 400px, focus ở tiêu đề): mỗi phím `←`/`→` cuộn các dòng lên đúng chiều cao tiêu đề (368, 336), `Tab` từ ngoài quay lại tiêu đề cuộn 129px (focus của chính trình duyệt, `preventScroll` không với tới: Chromium cuộn trước sự kiện focus, WebKit sau một hay nhiều khung hình), `focus()` của handle cuộn thêm 32px; Firefox không cuộn. Vì vậy phần chừa cho tiêu đề chuyển từ khung sang các dòng (như trên): với ô thân, phép tính của `nearest`, `start`, `center` cho cùng vị trí như phần đệm cũ, nên mọi cuộn tới ô thân và các ảnh chuẩn không đổi; ô tiêu đề ở chỗ nó dính đã nằm trong tầm nhìn, nên không lối nào (phím, `Tab`, `focus()`) cuộn dọc. `scroll-margin` âm trên ô tiêu đề cũng chạy ở cả ba engine nhưng dời hộp của tiêu đề cả với trang, nên tiêu đề ở trên mép cửa sổ sẽ bị cuộn ra ngoài, và việc hoàn lại lần cuộn của trình duyệt sau sự kiện focus thì không chắc (WebKit cuộn muộn hơn ba khung hình khi máy bận), nên không dùng. Ô tiêu đề cũng đi qua cùng `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })` như ô thân: khung không cuộn dọc vì tiêu đề dính đã ở trong tầm nhìn của khung, khung cuộn ngang theo `nearest`, và trang quanh grid đưa tiêu đề vào cửa sổ khi trang đã cuộn qua nó (có `height` hay không); một bản trước dùng `scrollLeft` tính tay cho tiêu đề (`scrollHeadIntoView`), nên tiêu đề tới bằng phím hay `focus()` có thể nằm ngoài cửa sổ, và đã bỏ (vòng sửa thứ hai của review PR #42).

Di chuyển bằng phím gọi `focus({ preventScroll: true })` rồi `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })` của **ô** (cả khi control trong ô giữ focus), cái tôn trọng `scroll-margin` của ô và `scroll-padding` của khung. Cuộn ảo: cuộn tới độ lệch tính được, render, rồi focus. **Đi trên tiêu đề không cuộn khung theo chiều dọc** (phát hiện khi review PR #42): tiêu đề dính ở đầu khung, trong `scroll-padding-top` của `Table`, và Chromium với WebKit coi phần đệm đó là phần che nó, nên đo bằng story `TitlesKeepScroll` (khung cuộn ở 400px, focus ở tiêu đề): mỗi phím `←`/`→` cuộn các dòng lên đúng chiều cao tiêu đề (368, 336), `Tab` từ ngoài quay lại tiêu đề cuộn 129px (focus của chính trình duyệt, `preventScroll` không với tới: Chromium cuộn trước sự kiện focus, WebKit sau một hay nhiều khung hình), `focus()` của handle cuộn thêm 32px; Firefox không cuộn. -- **Cột có `width`:** đúng số đó; grid không có cột co giãn nào thì bảng có thêm một **cột đệm** ở cuối: `<col>` không có `width`, và mỗi hàng một ô rỗng (`th` ở hàng tiêu đề; `td` ở dòng dữ liệu, dòng skeleton; `colspan` của dòng trống và hàng đệm của cuộn ảo tính cả nó) có `aria-hidden="true"`, không `tabindex`, lớp `flg-data-grid-filler` cùng lớp ô của `Table`, không padding. Bảng rộng bằng tổng các cột (`width` px) và ít nhất bằng khung (`min-width: 100%`), nên cột đệm lấy `max(0, bề rộng khung − tổng)` bằng CSS, không cần số đo (HTML từ server như nhau); không dùng `width: 100%` với `min-width` bằng tổng, vì Firefox không cho bảng `width: 100%` bề rộng nội tại nào, nên grid trong một hộp co theo nội dung (căn giữa bằng flex, `fit-content`) đóng lại còn 0px, khung hẹp hơn tổng thì vẫn cuộn ngang, và mọi cột thật giữ đúng độ rộng của nó (không có cột đệm thì trình duyệt chia phần thừa theo tỉ lệ cho mọi cột, và `width` thành tỉ lệ). Cột đệm không phải cột của grid: không có trong các cột đã chuẩn hoá, mũi tên, `Home`/`End`, `mod+End` không tới nó (`End` tới cột thật cuối), không bao giờ là ô hoạt động; con trỏ trên nó là trên dòng của nó (dòng vẫn hover), còn lần nhấn trên nó bị huỷ `mousedown` (focus ở nguyên chỗ, khung với `tabindex="-1"` không lấy nó) và không làm gì: không đổi ô hoạt động, không chọn dòng, nhấn đúp không gọi `onRowActivate` (vòng sửa sau review lại); nhưng nó mang những gì dòng vẽ trên bề rộng của nó (vạch của `lined`, nền hover và chọn, sọc và góc bo phải của `striped`, dải tiêu đề dính), nên mỗi dòng là một dải tới mép khung. Có cột co giãn thì không có cột đệm (phát hiện khi review cuối Plan B; chủ dự án chọn phương án E ngày 2026-11-17). Cột đệm chỉ có trong DOM khi khung đủ chỗ cho nó mang đầu cuối của dòng: khi khung chưa được đo (server, lần render đầu ở client, jsdom, grid bị ẩn: khung đo ra 0 không tính là đo) hoặc khi phần dư (bề rộng khung trừ thanh cuộn và padding, trừ tổng các cột) ít nhất là `max(1, độ bo)`; độ bo là `border-top-right-radius` đã tính (px) của ô cuối của dòng đầu tiên trong `.flg-table-body` của khung, không có dòng như thế hay giá trị không đọc được thì là 0. Vậy `lined` và `minimal` (độ bo 0) có cột đệm từ 1px dư, `striped` cần đủ độ bo (8px với token mặc định). Thiếu chỗ thì không có cột đệm: bảng rộng đúng tổng các cột (`width` và `min-width` bằng tổng, vì `width: 100%` của `Table` sẽ chia phần dư cho các cột), dòng `striped` kết thúc bo tròn cách mép khung vài px như trước phương án E, và mọi `colspan` (dòng trống, hàng đệm) không tính nó. Lý do: cột đệm 0px hay 2px vẫn là `:last-child` của dòng, nên lấy mất các quy tắc cho đầu cuối dòng của `Table` (góc bo phải của `striped`, cạnh phải của khung 2px quanh dòng chọn khi `prefers-contrast: more`). Grid đo khung bằng một `ResizeObserver` cả khi mọi cột có `width`, đọc lại độ bo khi `variant` hoặc `density` đổi và khi các dòng thay chỗ lời của grid rỗng (lời ấy không phải dòng để đọc), khung đo ra 0 thì giữ kết quả cũ. Ở client, effect bố cục quyết định trước lần vẽ đầu, nên không chớp; một trang hydrate thì những khung hình trước khi hydrate là HTML của server, có cột đệm, rồi lần commit của hydrate bỏ nó trước lần vẽ kế tiếp (phát hiện khi soát ảnh chuẩn PR #42). **Cột không có `width`** co giãn: chia đều phần còn lại của bề rộng khung (đo bằng `ResizeObserver`), không dưới `minWidth` (mặc định 60px). Khi có cột co giãn, bảng rộng `max(bề rộng khung, tổng các cột)` (phát hiện khi review cuối Plan B: câu này chỉ đúng khi có cột co giãn); rộng hơn khung thì khung cuộn ngang.

+## Pinned columns
+
+A column that is pinned to the left or to the right stays at that edge of the frame while the frame
+scrolls sideways, and the other columns go under it. `pinned: 'left'` on a column, or a `pinned`
+part of `defaultColumnLayout` or of `columnLayout`, says which (see Column layout: the layout decides
+where a column starts, and a later change of a column's own `pinned` does nothing). The zones are
+the first and the last columns of the grid in the order of the layout, so a pinned column is never
+in the middle of the row. The selection column of `selectionMode="multiple"` is pinned to the left
+when a data column is, and is not otherwise.
+
+```tsx
+<DataGrid
+  data={orders}
+  rowKey="id"
+  columns={columns}
+  selectionMode="multiple"
+  height={420}
+  defaultColumnLayout={{ pinned: { id: 'left', total: 'right' } }}
+/>
+```
+
+**What sticks, and when it is solid.** A pinned cell, in the heading and in every row, is
+transparent while nothing is scrolled under it, like every other cell: a grid at rest looks as it
+would without pins, with a line of 1px at the edge of each zone. When the frame has been scrolled
+away from an end, the zone at that end turns solid (`--flg-data-grid-pin-bg`), so what scrolls under
+it is not seen, and a shadow of 14px (`--flg-data-grid-pin-shadow`) is drawn beside its edge. The
+shadow is as tall as the part of the table the frame shows, and never reaches below the last row.
+The wash of a stripe, of the pointer and of a chosen row (and the bar of a chosen row of a `lined`
+grid) is drawn on a solid cell as on any other. The heading sticks at the top, over the pinned cells
+of the rows, as it does over the others. A `striped` or `minimal` frame has 6px of padding, inside
+which a sticky cell would stick; the grid takes that back, so no strip of cells that have scrolled
+shows beside a zone. In forced colours the pinned cells are `Canvas` and the line at the edge is a
+border in the text colour; the shadow and the washes are not drawn.
+
+The grid listens to the scroll of its frame, and measures it, only while a column is pinned, and a
+scroll draws nothing of the grid: it writes `data-scrolled-left` and `data-scrolled-right` on the
+frame, which the stylesheet reads.
+
+**Keys and scrolling.** The keys go across the zones as across any column, and a key onto a pinned
+cell scrolls nothing: the cell is where it is. A cell of the middle that a key, `focus()`, the
+handle's `focus()`, `scrollIntoView` or Tab brings into view stops clear of both zones, and not
+under them. That is done by a scroll margin, of the width of the zone, on the cells of the middle,
+and none on the pinned ones; the frame has no scroll padding at the sides.
+
+**A column without a width, pinned.** A pinned column needs its width to know where the next one
+sticks. Until the frame has been measured (on the server, in the first render) a column without a
+`width` counts its `minWidth`, a lower bound, so no cell sticks to the right of where it rests in
+the HTML of the server; after the frame is measured it counts the pixels it was given.
+
+**The filler column** (see Widths) goes before the right zone, so that the zone ends the row at the
+edge of the frame. It is still no column: the keys, Home and End go across it, and a press on it does
+nothing.
+

+/**
+ * How far each shown column sticks from the edge of the frame: for a column of the left zone the
+ * sum of the widths of the zone before it, for one of the right zone the sum of the widths after it,
+ * and `undefined` for the columns in between, which do not stick. `widths` are the widths of the
+ * shown columns, the column of boxes first; the filler column is no column, and has none.
+ */
+export function pinOffsets(
+  widths: readonly number[],
+  pins: readonly (DataGridPin | undefined)[],
+): (number | undefined)[] {
+  let left = 0;
+  const offsets = pins.map((pin, index) => {
+    if (pin !== 'left') return undefined;
+    const offset = left;
+    left += widths[index] ?? 0;
+    return offset;
+  });
+  let right = 0;
+  for (let index = pins.length - 1; index >= 0; index--) {
+    if (pins[index] !== 'right') continue;
+    offsets[index] = right;
+    right += widths[index] ?? 0;
+  }
+  return offsets;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Where the filler column goes among the shown columns: before the right zone, so that the zone
+ * ends the row at the edge of the frame (the filler takes what the columns leave), and at the end
+ * of the row when no column is pinned to the right (spec phase 6 §3.7).
+ */
+export function fillerIndex(pins: readonly (DataGridPin | undefined)[]): number {
+  const first = pins.indexOf('right');
+  return first < 0 ? pins.length : first;
+}
+
+/**

+ * next to the middle (the last of the left zone, the first of the right zone: it draws the edge
+ * line and the shadow), and the style that sticks it. The offset is a custom property of the table
+ * (`--flg-data-grid-pin-<i>`, written with the widths), so a change of a width changes the table and
+ * not the cells.
+ */
+export interface PinPlace {
+  side: DataGridPin;
+  edge: boolean;
+  style: { left: string } | { right: string };
+}
+
+/** The place of each shown column among the zones; `undefined` for a column in the middle. */
+export function pinPlaces(pins: readonly (DataGridPin | undefined)[]): (PinPlace | undefined)[] {
+  const lastLeft = pins.lastIndexOf('left');
+  const firstRight = pins.indexOf('right');

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-pinned-scroll.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-pinned-scroll.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8572cca
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-pinned-scroll.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+import type { RefObject } from 'react';
+import { useIsoLayoutEffect } from '../../../internal/use-iso-layout-effect';
+
+/** The custom property of the frame that holds how tall the shadow of a pinned zone is. */
+export const VIEW_HEIGHT_PROPERTY = '--flg-data-grid-view-height';
+
+const SCROLLED_LEFT = 'data-scrolled-left';
+const SCROLLED_RIGHT = 'data-scrolled-right';
+
+/**
+ * How tall the part of the table that the frame shows is, from the top of the heading to the end of
+ * the last row or the bottom of the frame, whichever is first: the shadow of a pinned zone is that
+ * tall, so it never hangs below the last row into the empty part of a frame with a `height`. The
+ * heading sticks to the top of the frame (a `striped` frame has padding, the heading sticks above
+ * it), so the table starts at its own top or at the top of the frame, whichever is lower. Sizes in
+ * layout pixels, which a transform does not change.
+ */
+function shownHeight(frame: HTMLElement, table: HTMLElement | null): number {
+  const start = table?.offsetTop ?? 0;
+  const top = Math.max(0, start - frame.scrollTop);
+  const bottom = Math.min(frame.clientHeight, start + (table?.offsetHeight ?? 0) - frame.scrollTop);
+  return Math.max(0, bottom - top);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Tells the stylesheet which sides of the frame have columns scrolled under a pinned zone (spec
+ * phase 6 §3.7): `data-scrolled-left` while the frame is scrolled from its left end, and
+ * `data-scrolled-right` while it is not at its right end. A pinned cell is solid only on a scrolled
+ * side, and the shadow of the edge of its zone is drawn only there, so a grid at rest draws neither.
+ * With a side scrolled, the height of the shadow is written as `--flg-data-grid-view-height`.
+ *
+ * The attributes and the property are written on the frame directly, and only when a value changes:
+ * a scroll draws no part of the grid. There is a listener and an observer only while a column is
+ * pinned (`enabled`), and they and what they wrote go with the last pin and with the grid. Nothing is
+ * measured of the table's height while no side is scrolled. After mount only: the server draws the
+ * grid at rest.
+ */
+export function usePinnedScroll(
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
+  tableRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
+  enabled: boolean,
+): void {
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const frame = frameRef.current;
+    if (!enabled || !frame) return undefined;
+    let left = false;
+    let right = false;
+    let height: string | null = null;
+    const set = (name: string, on: boolean) => {
+      if (on) frame.setAttribute(name, '');
+      else frame.removeAttribute(name);
+    };
+    const update = () => {
+      const nextLeft = frame.scrollLeft > 0;
+      // A pixel short of the end is the end: a fraction of a pixel is no scroll.
+      const nextRight = frame.scrollLeft + frame.clientWidth < frame.scrollWidth - 1;
+      if (nextLeft !== left) set(SCROLLED_LEFT, (left = nextLeft));
+      if (nextRight !== right) set(SCROLLED_RIGHT, (right = nextRight));
+      const next = left || right ? `${shownHeight(frame, tableRef.current)}px` : null;
+      if (next === height) return;
+      height = next;
+      if (next === null) frame.style.removeProperty(VIEW_HEIGHT_PROPERTY);
+      else frame.style.setProperty(VIEW_HEIGHT_PROPERTY, next);
+    };
+    update();
+    frame.addEventListener('scroll', update, { passive: true });
+    const observer = typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined' ? undefined : new ResizeObserver(update);
+    observer?.observe(frame);
+    if (tableRef.current) observer?.observe(tableRef.current);
+    return () => {
+      frame.removeEventListener('scroll', update);
+      observer?.disconnect();
+      frame.removeAttribute(SCROLLED_LEFT);
+      frame.removeAttribute(SCROLLED_RIGHT);
+      frame.style.removeProperty(VIEW_HEIGHT_PROPERTY);
+    };
+  }, [frameRef, tableRef, enabled]);
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/pin-attributes.ts b/src/components/data-grid/parts/pin-attributes.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ccb0c36
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/pin-attributes.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+import { dataAttr } from '../../../internal/data-attr';
+import type { PinPlace } from '../engine/layout';
+
+const NOT_PINNED = {};
+
+/**
+ * What a cell of a pinned column has on it: the side it sticks to, whether it is the edge of its
+ * zone, and the style that sticks it (`left` or `right`, a custom property that the table writes).
+ * The cell is made sticky by the stylesheet, which reads these; a column in the middle has nothing.
+ */
+export function pinAttributes(place: PinPlace | undefined) {
+  if (!place) return NOT_PINNED;
+  return {
+    'data-pinned': place.side,
+    'data-pin-edge': dataAttr(place.edge),
+    style: place.style,
+  };
+}

+// grid that holds its own layout renders itself once for that, which is its state changing.

+    renders.toolbar = 0;
+    renders.body = 0;

+        data={ORDERS.slice(0, 5)}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={COLUMNS}
+        caption="Orders"
+        paging={false}
+        {...props}
+      />,
+    );
+    // jsdom has no layout: the frame is wide, so the pointer is never at its edge.
+    const frame = grid().parentElement!;
+    frame.getBoundingClientRect = () =>
+      ({ left: 0, top: 0, right: 10000, bottom: 10000, width: 0, height: 0 }) as DOMRect;
+    const handle = grid().tHead!.rows[0]!.cells[1]!.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-resizer')!;

+    fireEvent.pointerDown(handle, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: 300, clientY: 10 });
+    for (const x of [310, 320, 330, 340, 350]) {
+      fireEvent.pointerMove(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: x, clientY: 10 });
+      act(() => {
+        for (const run of frames.splice(0)) run();
+      });

+      this: HTMLElement,
+    ) {
+      return this.classList.contains('flg-table-frame') ? 900 : 0;
+    });

+      { columns: COLUMNS.map((column) => ({ ...column, width: undefined })) },
+      '350px',
+    );
+    expect(moves).toEqual({ headerCell: 0, toolbar: 0, body: 0, cell: 0 });
+    expect(release).toEqual({ headerCell: 0, toolbar: 1, body: 1, cell: 0 });
+  });
+});
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.resize.test.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.resize.test.tsx

@@ -0,0 +1,919 @@
+import { act, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { createRef } from 'react';
+import type { Ref } from 'react';
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { resetDevWarnings } from '../../internal/warn';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type {
+  DataGridColumn,
+  DataGridColumnLayout,
+  DataGridHandle,
+  DataGridProps,
+  DataGridState,
+} from './index';
+
+// Resizing the columns (spec phase 6 §3.7, §3.8, §6.3 "Đổi độ rộng"): the handle, the drag, the live
+// widths, the freeze of the flexible columns, the release, the keys, the double press that fits, and
+// what the grid sets and takes off while a drag is in flight. What needs a layout engine to be true
+// (the guide's box, a fit against real text, no text selected, a real mouse) is proven in the stories
+// (`DataGridColumns.stories.tsx`).
+
+// The animation frames the drag asks for (the coalesced moves, the auto-scroll), run by hand.
+let frames: Map<number, FrameRequestCallback>;
+let nextFrame: number;
+const runFrames = () => {
+  const due = [...frames.values()];
+  frames.clear();
+  act(() => due.forEach((callback) => callback(0)));
+};
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  frames = new Map();
+  nextFrame = 1;
+  vi.stubGlobal('requestAnimationFrame', (callback: FrameRequestCallback) => {
+    frames.set(nextFrame, callback);
+    return nextFrame++;
+  });
+  vi.stubGlobal('cancelAnimationFrame', (id: number) => frames.delete(id));
+  // jsdom has no layout, so every element would count as hidden to the code that looks for the
+  // controls of a cell.
+  HTMLElement.prototype.checkVisibility = () => true;
+  // jsdom has no layout: every box is where the pointer of a test is, wide, with no size of its own, so
+  // the frame does not scroll under it (a test of the auto-scroll gives the frame its own box).
+  vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockReturnValue({
+    left: 0,
+    top: 0,
+    right: 10000,
+    bottom: 10000,
+    width: 0,
+    height: 0,
+    x: 0,
+    y: 0,
+    toJSON: () => ({}),
+  });
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'checkVisibility');
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+  vi.useRealTimers();
+  document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-flg-grid-cursor');
+});
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  qty: number;
+  total: number;
+}
+
+const ORDERS: Order[] = [
+  { id: 'DH-1030', customer: 'Nguyễn Minh', qty: 4, total: 1250000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1029', customer: 'Trần Hải', qty: 1, total: 890000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1028', customer: 'Lê An', qty: 12, total: 15400000 },
+];
+
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+  { field: 'total', caption: 'Total', dataType: 'number', width: 120 },
+];
+const FLEXIBLE: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = COLUMNS.map((column) => ({
+  ...column,
+  width: undefined,
+}));
+
+const WIDTHS = { id: 104, customer: 200, qty: 80, total: 120 };
+
+function Orders({
+  handleRef,
+  ...props
+}: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>> & { handleRef?: Ref<DataGridHandle> }) {
+  return (
+    <DataGrid
+      ref={handleRef}
+      data={ORDERS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={false}
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+const grid = () => screen.getByRole('grid') as HTMLTableElement;
+const frame = () => grid().parentElement as HTMLElement;
+// The titles of the columns: the filler column's is none.
+const titles = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().tHead!.rows[0]!.cells).filter(
+    (cell) => !cell.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-filler'),
+  );
+const title = (name: string) => titles().find((cell) => cell.textContent?.includes(name))!;
+const handleOf = (name: string) =>
+  title(name).querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-resizer') as HTMLElement;
+const cols = () => Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('col'));
+const widthOf = (index: number) => cols()[index]!.style.width;
+const html = () => document.documentElement;
+
+const POINTER = { pointerId: 1, isPrimary: true, pointerType: 'mouse', button: 0 };
+const press = (element: Element, x: number, init: PointerEventInit = {}) =>
+  fireEvent.pointerDown(element, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: x, clientY: 10, ...init });
+// A move with the main button down, as every move of a press is.
+const move = (x: number, init: PointerEventInit = {}) =>
+  fireEvent.pointerMove(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: x, clientY: 10, ...init });
+const release = (x: number) =>
+  fireEvent.pointerUp(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 0, clientX: x, clientY: 10 });
+
+/** A drag of a handle by `dx` from where it is pressed, released there. */
+function drag(handle: Element, dx: number, startX = 300) {
+  press(handle, startX);
+  move(startX + dx);
+  runFrames();
+  release(startX + dx);
+}
+
+describe('the handle', () => {
+  it('is the last child of the title of each column that can be resized', () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    const handles = titles().map((cell) => cell.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-resizer'));
+    expect(handles).toHaveLength(4);
+    for (const [index, handle] of handles.entries()) {
+      expect(handle, `title ${index}`).not.toBeNull();
+      expect(handle).toBe(titles()[index]!.lastElementChild);
+      expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
+      expect(handle).not.toHaveAttribute('tabindex');
+    }
+  });
+
+  it('is on no title of a grid that turns resizing off, and on those columns that turn it on', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders allowResizing={false} />);
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('.flg-data-grid-resizer')).toHaveLength(0);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders
+        allowResizing={false}
+        columns={COLUMNS.map((column, index) => ({ ...column, allowResizing: index === 1 }))}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('.flg-data-grid-resizer')).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(handleOf('Customer')).not.toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('is on no title of a column that turns resizing off', () => {
+    render(
+      <Orders
+        columns={COLUMNS.map((column) => ({ ...column, allowResizing: column.field !== 'qty' }))}
+      />,
+    );
+    expect(title('Qty').querySelector('.flg-data-grid-resizer')).toBeNull();
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('.flg-data-grid-resizer')).toHaveLength(3);
+  });
+
+  it('is not on the title of the column of boxes', () => {
+    render(<Orders selectionMode="multiple" />);
+    expect(titles()[0]!.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-resizer')).toBeNull();
+    expect(grid().querySelectorAll('.flg-data-grid-resizer')).toHaveLength(4);
+  });
+
+  it('cancels the mousedown of a press and focuses the title, and sorts nothing', () => {
+    const onSortChange = vi.fn();
+    render(<Orders onSortChange={onSortChange} />);
+    const customer = title('Customer');
+    expect(document.activeElement).not.toBe(customer);
+    const proceeded = fireEvent.mouseDown(handleOf('Customer'), { button: 0 });
+    expect(proceeded).toBe(false);
+    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(customer);
+    fireEvent.click(handleOf('Customer'));
+    expect(onSortChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('leaves the mousedown of the other buttons alone', () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    expect(fireEvent.mouseDown(handleOf('Customer'), { button: 2 })).toBe(true);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('dragging a handle', () => {
+  it('writes the width of the column on its <col> as the pointer moves, held to its least width', () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('200px');
+    press(handleOf('Customer'), 300);
+    move(340);
+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('240px');
+    move(250);
+    runFrames();
+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('150px');
+    move(-500);
+    runFrames();
+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('60px');
+    move(9000);
+    runFrames();
+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('2000px');
+    release(9000);
+  });
+
+  it('holds the width to the minWidth of the column, and the table is as wide as the columns', () => {
+    render(<Orders columns={COLUMNS.map((column) => ({ ...column, minWidth: 90 }))} />);
+    press(handleOf('Customer'), 300);
+    move(100);
+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('90px');
+    expect(grid().style.width).toBe('394px');
+    release(100);
+  });
+
+  it('does not start under the threshold of 4px, and is then a click', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    render(<Orders onColumnLayoutChange={onColumnLayoutChange} />);
+    press(handleOf('Customer'), 300);

+    release(302);

+  it('calls onColumnLayoutChange once, at the release, with the layout as shown', () => {

+    const layout: DataGridColumnLayout = {

+  it('puts the width in what getState() gives', () => {

+  it('calls nothing for a drag that ends where it began, and the layout stays', () => {

+  });
+
+  it('is cancelled by pointercancel: the live width goes and nothing is called', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    render(<Orders onColumnLayoutChange={onColumnLayoutChange} />);

+

+    press(handleOf('Customer'), 300);
+    move(360);

+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('260px');
+    fireEvent(
+      handleOf('Customer'),
+      Object.assign(new Event('lostpointercapture'), { pointerId: 1 }),
+    );
+    expect(widthOf(1)).toBe('200px');
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('ends quietly at a move with no button down before the threshold, which is a release that was lost', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    render(<Orders onColumnLayoutChange={onColumnLayoutChange} />);
+    press(handleOf('Customer'), 300);

+    move(380);

+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

+
+  it('ends at a move with no button down after it started, with the width the pointer had', () => {

+describe('the widths of columns that have none', () => {

+// ---- Resizing the columns (spec phase 6 §3.7, §3.8, §4.3 C1) -------------------------------------------
+
+/** A distance in layout pixels: engines round a box, and a pointer may be a fraction away. */
+const near = (actual: number, expected: number, within = 1.5, what = 'distance') =>
+  expect(Math.abs(actual - expected), `${what}: ${actual} against ${expected}`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(
+    within,
+  );
+
+const titleCell = (root: HTMLElement, caption: string) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('th.flg-data-grid-head')).find((cell) =>
+    cell.textContent?.includes(caption),
+  )!;
+const handleOf = (root: HTMLElement, caption: string) =>
+  titleCell(root, caption).querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-resizer')!;
+
+/** No title is cut: a later part of a heading that takes room cannot cut one without a story failing. */
+const noTitleIsCut = async (root: HTMLElement) => {
+  const titles = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-head-title'));
+  await expect(titles.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+  for (const title of titles)
+    await expect(title.scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(title.clientWidth);
+};
+
+/** A drag with the real mouse: down on the handle, to `dx` away from where it is, up. */
+async function dragBy(real: RealUserEvent, root: HTMLElement, caption: string, dx: number) {
+  const handle = handleOf(root, caption);
+  const frame = frameOf(root);
+  const at = handle.getBoundingClientRect();
+  const box = frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+  await real.dragAndDrop(handle, frame, {
+    targetPosition: {
+      // Relative to the padding box of the frame, which is inside its border.
+      x: at.left + at.width / 2 + dx - (box.left + frame.clientLeft),
+      y: at.top + at.height / 2 - (box.top + frame.clientTop),
+    },
+  });
+  await frames();
+}
+
+/**
+ * A pointer the browser does not know, for the states of a drag that need the button held: a real
+ * button cannot be left down from a play function, and the listeners of the page follow a pointer of
+ * any id all the same (as the Dialog's stories do). The layout and the stylesheet are the browser's.
+ */
+function pointer(type: 'mouse' | 'touch', id: number, from: { x: number; y: number }) {
+  return (target: EventTarget, name: string, dx: number) =>
+    target.dispatchEvent(
+      new PointerEvent(name, {
+        bubbles: true,
+        cancelable: true,
+        pointerId: id,
+        isPrimary: true,
+        pointerType: type,
+        button: 0,
+        buttons: name === 'pointerup' ? 0 : 1,
+        clientX: from.x + dx,
+        clientY: from.y,
+      }),
+    );
+}
+const middleOf = (element: Element) => {
+  const box = element.getBoundingClientRect();
+  return { x: box.left + box.width / 2, y: box.top + box.height / 2 };
+};

+/** A grid narrower than its columns, with a height, for the drags: five columns that have a width. */

+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'assignee', caption: 'Assignee', width: 160 },
+  { field: 'date', caption: 'Order date', dataType: 'date', width: 130 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+];
+const ResizeGrid = (props: Partial<DataGridProps<Sale>>) => (
+  <div style={{ width: 640 }}>
