```diff
+      aria-label="Orders"
+      data={SALES.slice(0, 8)}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={RESIZE_COLUMNS}
+      height={300}
+      paging={false}
+      locale="vi-VN"
+      {...props}
+    />
+  </div>
+);
+
+/**
+ * Resizing with a real mouse, in each engine: a drag of the handle makes the column as wide as the
+ * pointer says and calls `onColumnLayoutChange` once, at the drop; the drop is not a click, so no sort,
+ * and the press selects no text. While a drag is held (pointer events the browser does not know, since
+ * a button cannot be left down), the guide runs from the bottom of the handle to the bottom of what the
+ * frame shows, at the middle of the handle, and the label that says the width is 10px under the handle
+ * and 6px left of the middle of the guide; the page has the cursor of the drag. Escape, which is real,
+ * puts the column back. A finger, which is emulated, drags too.
+ */
+export const ResizingColumns: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  args: { onColumnLayoutChange: fn(), onSortChange: fn() },
+  render: (args) => (
+    <ResizeGrid onColumnLayoutChange={args.onColumnLayoutChange} onSortChange={args.onSortChange} />
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const table = tableOf(root);
+    const frame = frameOf(root);
+    const html = document.documentElement;
+    const customer = () => titleCell(root, 'Customer');
+    await expect(customer().offsetWidth).toBe(200);
+    await noTitleIsCut(root);
+
+    // The real mouse: wider, then narrower. Each drop is one change, and no press sorted or selected.
+    await dragBy(real, root, 'Customer', 40);
+    near(customer().offsetWidth, 240, 1, 'wider');
+    await expect(args.onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    await dragBy(real, root, 'Customer', -30);
+    near(customer().offsetWidth, 210, 1, 'narrower');
+    await expect(args.onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
+    await expect(args.onSortChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    await expect(table.querySelector('[aria-sort]')).toBeNull();
+    await expect(getSelection()?.toString()).toBe('');
+    await expect(html).not.toHaveAttribute('data-flg-grid-cursor');
+    await expect(handleOf(root, 'Customer')).not.toHaveAttribute('data-dragging');
+    await expect(root.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-resize-guide')).toBeNull();
+
+    // A drag that is held: the guide and the label stand where the spec says, the page has the cursor.
+    const assignee = handleOf(root, 'Assignee');
+    const start = middleOf(assignee);
+    const send = pointer('mouse', 31, start);
+    const wasWide = titleCell(root, 'Assignee').offsetWidth;
+    send(assignee, 'pointerdown', 0);
+    send(document, 'pointermove', 30);
+    await waitFor(() => expect(root.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-resize-guide')).not.toBeNull());
+    await frames();
+    near(titleCell(root, 'Assignee').offsetWidth, wasWide + 30, 1, 'live width');
+    const guide = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-resize-guide')!;
+    const pill = guide.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-width-pill')!;
+    const at = guide.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const handle = assignee.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const shown = frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const centre = at.left + at.width / 2;
+    near(centre, handle.left + handle.width / 2, 1.5, 'the guide is at the middle of the handle');
+    near(at.width, 2, 0.5, 'the guide is 2px wide');
+    near(at.top, handle.bottom, 1.5, 'the guide starts at the bottom of the handle');
+    near(
+      at.bottom,
+      shown.top + frame.clientTop + frame.clientHeight,
+      1.5,
+      'the guide ends at the bottom of what the frame shows',
+    );
+    const label = pill.getBoundingClientRect();
+    near(label.top, handle.bottom + 10, 1.5, 'the label is 10px under the handle');
+    near(label.right, centre - 6, 1.5, 'the label is 6px left of the middle of the guide');
+    await expect(pill).toHaveTextContent(`${titleCell(root, 'Assignee').offsetWidth} px`);
+    await expect(getComputedStyle(guide).pointerEvents).toBe('none');
+    await expect(getComputedStyle(pill).pointerEvents).toBe('none');
+    await expect(html).toHaveAttribute('data-flg-grid-cursor', 'col-resize');
+    await expect(getComputedStyle(table.tBodies[0]!.rows[0]!.cells[1]!).cursor).toBe('col-resize');
+    await expect(assignee).toHaveAttribute('data-dragging');
+    // The handle's bar is the accent, 3px wide, all the height of the title, while it is dragged.
+    const bar = getComputedStyle(assignee, '::before');
+    await expect(bar.width).toBe('3px');
+    near(Number.parseFloat(bar.height), titleCell(root, 'Assignee').clientHeight, 1, 'the bar');
+
+    // Escape, a real key, cancels: the column is as it was, nothing was called, the page is let go.
+    const calls = (args.onColumnLayoutChange as ReturnType<typeof fn>).mock.calls.length;
+    await real.keyboard('{Escape}');
+    await frames();
+    near(titleCell(root, 'Assignee').offsetWidth, wasWide, 1, 'after Escape');
+    await expect(args.onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(calls);
+    await expect(root.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-resize-guide')).toBeNull();
+    await expect(html).not.toHaveAttribute('data-flg-grid-cursor');
+    await expect(assignee).not.toHaveAttribute('data-dragging');
+    send(document, 'pointerup', 30);
+    await frames();
+    near(titleCell(root, 'Assignee').offsetWidth, wasWide, 1, 'the release after Escape');
+
+    // A finger: the same drag, with a pointer of type `touch`, which the runner does not emulate.
+    const finger = pointer('touch', 32, middleOf(handleOf(root, 'Order date')));
+    const wasDate = titleCell(root, 'Order date').offsetWidth;
+    finger(handleOf(root, 'Order date'), 'pointerdown', 0);
+    finger(document, 'pointermove', 25);
+    finger(document, 'pointerup', 25);
+    await frames();
+    near(titleCell(root, 'Order date').offsetWidth, wasDate + 25, 1, 'by touch');
+    await expect(args.onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(calls + 1);
+    await noTitleIsCut(root);
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * The keys, which are the same on both platforms: <kbd>Alt+Shift+→</kbd> three times on a title makes
+ * its column 30px wider, one change of the layout for each press, and the new width is said once, after
+ * the last of them. A held key does not scroll the frame.
+ */
+const resizeKeys: NonNullable<Story['play']> = async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+  const real = await realUserEvent();
+  if (!real) return;
+  const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+  const frame = frameOf(root);
+  const customer = () => titleCell(root, 'Customer');
+  // Tab lands on the first cell of the first row; the title of Customer is up and along.
+  await real.tab();
+  await real.keyboard('{ArrowUp}{ArrowRight}');
+  await expect(customer()).toHaveFocus();
+  const said: string[] = [];
+  const region = root.querySelector('[aria-live="polite"]')!;
+  const watcher = new MutationObserver(() => {
+    if (region.textContent) said.push(region.textContent);
+  });
+  watcher.observe(region, { childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true });
+  const scroll = { left: frame.scrollLeft, top: frame.scrollTop };
+  for (const width of [210, 220, 230]) {
+    await real.keyboard('{Alt>}{Shift>}{ArrowRight}{/Shift}{/Alt}');
+    await expect(customer().offsetWidth).toBe(width);
+  }
+  await expect(args.onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
+  await expect(customer()).toHaveFocus();
+  await expect({ left: frame.scrollLeft, top: frame.scrollTop }).toEqual(scroll);
+  await real.keyboard('{Alt>}{Shift>}{ArrowLeft}{/Shift}{/Alt}');
+  await expect(customer().offsetWidth).toBe(220);
+  // Said once, a moment after the last press.
+  await waitFor(() => expect(said).toEqual(['Customer, 220 pixels wide']), { timeout: 3000 });
+  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 700));
+  await expect(said).toEqual(['Customer, 220 pixels wide']);
+  watcher.disconnect();
+  await noTitleIsCut(root);
+};
+
+export const ResizeKeys: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('other'),
+  args: { onColumnLayoutChange: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <ResizeGrid onColumnLayoutChange={args.onColumnLayoutChange} />,
+  play: resizeKeys,
+};
+
+export const ResizeKeysOnAMac: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('apple'),
+  args: { onColumnLayoutChange: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <ResizeGrid onColumnLayoutChange={args.onColumnLayoutChange} />,
+  play: resizeKeys,
+};
+
+/**
+ * A double press on a handle fits the column to what its title and its drawn cells need, in each
+ * engine: a column that is too wide shrinks to the longest text, a column that cuts its text grows to
+ * it, and no cell is cut after. The width is the text, the padding of the cell, and nothing more than a
+ * pixel. It is one change of the layout each, and the press sorts nothing.
+ */
+export const FittingColumns: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  args: { onColumnLayoutChange: fn(), onSortChange: fn() },
+  render: (args) => (
+    <div style={{ width: 760 }}>
+      <DataGrid
+        aria-label="Orders"
+        data={PAGE_ONE}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={[
+          { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 100 },
+          { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 420 },
+          { field: 'assignee', caption: 'Assignee', width: 60 },
+        ]}
+        allowSorting={false}
+        paging={false}
+        onColumnLayoutChange={args.onColumnLayoutChange}
+        onSortChange={args.onSortChange}
+      />
+    </div>
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const table = tableOf(root);
+    const cellsOfColumn = (index: number) =>
+      Array.from(table.tBodies[0]!.rows, (row) => row.cells[index] as HTMLTableCellElement);
+
+    /** The width of the longest text of a column, measured by a probe that has the cell's own font. */
+    const longestText = (index: number) => {
+      const cells = cellsOfColumn(index);
+      const style = getComputedStyle(cells[0]!);
+      const probe = document.createElement('span');
+      probe.style.cssText = `position:absolute;visibility:hidden;white-space:nowrap;font-family:${style.fontFamily};font-size:${style.fontSize};font-weight:${style.fontWeight};font-style:${style.fontStyle};font-variant-numeric:${style.fontVariantNumeric};letter-spacing:${style.letterSpacing}`;
+      document.body.append(probe);
+      const widest = Math.max(
+        ...cells.map((cell) => {
+          probe.textContent = cell.textContent;
+          return probe.getBoundingClientRect().width;
+        }),
+      );
+      probe.remove();
+      return {
+        text: widest,
+        padding: Number.parseFloat(style.paddingLeft) + Number.parseFloat(style.paddingRight),
+      };
+    };
+
+    await expect(cellsOfColumn(1).some((cell) => cell.scrollWidth > cell.clientWidth)).toBe(false);
+    await expect(cellsOfColumn(2).some((cell) => cell.scrollWidth > cell.clientWidth)).toBe(true);
+
+    for (const [index, caption] of [
+      [1, 'Customer'],
+      [2, 'Assignee'],
+    ] as const) {
+      const was = args.onColumnLayoutChange as ReturnType<typeof fn>;
+      const before = was.mock.calls.length;
+      await real.dblClick(handleOf(root, caption));
+      await frames();
+      await expect(was).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(before + 1);
+      const { text, padding } = longestText(index);
+      const column = titleCell(root, caption).offsetWidth;
+      near(column, Math.ceil(text) + padding, 1.5, `${caption} fits its longest text`);
+      for (const cell of cellsOfColumn(index)) {
+        await expect(cell.scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(cell.clientWidth + 1);
+      }
+    }
+    await expect(args.onSortChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    await expect(table.querySelector('[aria-sort]')).toBeNull();
+    await noTitleIsCut(root);
+  },
+};
+
+// ---- Look stories: the column parts of C1 (spec phase 6 §4.3 C1, mockup phase-6-grid.html) -----------
+
+/** A column of G1 at the width of the crops of C1. */
+const cropColumn = (field: keyof Sale & string, width: number): DataGridColumn<Sale> => ({
+  ...SALE_COLUMNS.find((column) => 'field' in column && column.field === field)!,
+  width,
+});
+
+/** The columns of the crops a and b of C1: Order 100, Customer 160, Assignee 190, Order date 130, Status 140. */
+const CROP_COLUMNS = [
+  cropColumn('id', 100),
+  cropColumn('customer', 160),
+  cropColumn('assignee', 190),
+  cropColumn('date', 130),
+  cropColumn('status', 140),
+];
+/** DH-1024, DH-1025 and DH-1026, in that order, as the crops show them. */
+const CROP_ROWS = ['DH-1024', 'DH-1025', 'DH-1026'].map((id) =>
+  SALES.find((order) => order.id === id)!,
+);
+
+/**
+ * A crop of C1: a surface of 634px with 10px of padding around a grid whose titles are plain (the crops
+ * draw no sort), cut at the right edge of the frame as the crop is. The frame's scrollbar is hidden, as
+ * the mockup draws a scroll without one: a classic scrollbar would narrow the frame and make it scroll.
+ */
+const CropGrid = ({ label }: { label: string }) => (
+  <div
+    className="flg-surface c1-crop"
+    style={{
+      width: 634,
+      boxSizing: 'border-box',
+      padding: 10,
+      borderRadius: 'var(--flg-radius-lg)',
+    }}
+  >
+    <style>{'.c1-crop .flg-table-frame { scrollbar-width: none; }'}</style>
+    <DataGrid
+      aria-label={label}
+      data={CROP_ROWS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={CROP_COLUMNS}
+      allowSorting={false}
+      paging={false}
+      locale="vi-VN"
+    />
+  </div>
+);
+
+/** What both crops are measured against in the mockup: the boxes of the titles and of the handle. */
+async function cropBoxes(root: HTMLElement) {
+  const widths = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('th.flg-data-grid-head'), (cell) =>
+    Math.round(cell.offsetWidth),
+  );
+  await expect(widths).toEqual([100, 160, 190, 130, 140]);
+  const handles = root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-resizer');
+  await expect(handles).toHaveLength(5);
+  for (const handle of handles) {
+    const box = handle.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const title = handle.closest('th')!.getBoundingClientRect();
+    near(box.width, 10, 0.5, 'the handle is 10px wide');
+    near(box.height, title.height - 1, 1, 'the handle is the height of the title, less its border');
+  }
+  await noTitleIsCut(root);
+}
+
+/**
+ * C1, crop a: the thin line between the titles at rest (left), and the bar of 3px in the accent on the
+ * handle between Customer and Assignee when the pointer is over it (right; the harness hovers what has
+ * `data-visual-hover`). Not drawn here, as in the other crops of C: nothing, the crops hold the column
+ * parts only. The last title of the crop is cut by the frame, as in the mockup.
+ */
+export const ColumnResizeHandle: Story = {
+  tags: ['viewport-1440x720'],
+  render: () => (
+    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 16, width: 1284 }}>
+      <CropGrid label="At rest" />
+      <CropGrid label="Hovered" />
+    </div>
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const roots = canvasElement.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid');
+    await expect(roots).toHaveLength(2);
+    for (const root of roots) await cropBoxes(root);
+    // The thin line at rest: 1px by 14px.
+    const line = getComputedStyle(handleOf(roots[0]!, 'Customer'), '::before');
+    await expect([line.width, line.height]).toEqual(['1px', '14px']);
+    handleOf(roots[1]!, 'Customer').setAttribute('data-visual-hover', '');
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * C1, crop b: Customer dragged from 160 to 180px (the harness drags what has `data-visual-drag` by
+ * the distance it says, and shoots with the button down): the bar of 3px, the guide down the frame
+ * and the label "180 px".
+ */
+export const ColumnResizing: Story = {
+  tags: ['viewport-1440x720'],
+  render: () => (
+    <div style={{ width: 634 }}>
+      <CropGrid label="Resizing" />
+    </div>
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    await cropBoxes(root);
+    handleOf(root, 'Customer').setAttribute('data-visual-drag', '20,0');
+  },
+};

+describe('clampWidth', () => {
+  it('holds a width to the minimum of the column and to 2000', () => {
+    expect(clampWidth(150, 60)).toBe(150);
+    expect(clampWidth(20, 60)).toBe(60);
+    expect(clampWidth(-300, 60)).toBe(60);
+    expect(clampWidth(5000, 60)).toBe(2000);
+  });
+
+  it('gives whole pixels, and never a width under a minimum that has a fraction', () => {
+    expect(clampWidth(150.4, 60)).toBe(150);
+    expect(clampWidth(150.6, 60)).toBe(151);
+    expect(clampWidth(10, 60.5)).toBe(61);
+  });
+
+  it('is the minimum for a width that is no number', () => {
+    expect(clampWidth(Number.NaN, 60)).toBe(60);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('autoFitWidth', () => {
+  it('is the widest of the measures, rounded up', () => {
+    expect(autoFitWidth([80, 143.2, 120], 60)).toBe(144);
+  });
+
+  it('is held to the minimum width of the column and to 600', () => {
+    expect(MAX_FIT_WIDTH).toBe(600);
+    expect(autoFitWidth([20, 30], 60)).toBe(60);
+    expect(autoFitWidth([900], 60)).toBe(600);
+  });
+
+  it('is the minimum width when there is nothing to measure', () => {
+    expect(autoFitWidth([], 75)).toBe(75);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps a minimum width that is over 600', () => {
+    expect(autoFitWidth([700], 640)).toBe(640);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('freezeWidths', () => {
+  const shown = [
+    { id: 'a', minWidth: 60, size: 100 },
+    { id: 'b', minWidth: 60, size: 233 },
+    { id: 'c', minWidth: 80, size: 311 },
+  ];
+
+  it('writes the measured width of every flexible column and the width of the one dragged', () => {
+    expect(freezeWidths({ a: 100 }, shown, 'b', 250)).toEqual({ a: 100, b: 250, c: 311 });
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the width a layout has, whatever the column measures now', () => {
+    expect(freezeWidths({ a: 90, b: 200, c: 300 }, shown, 'a', 120)).toEqual({
+      a: 120,
+      b: 200,
+      c: 300,
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('holds a flexible column that was not measured to its minimum width', () => {
+    expect(
+      freezeWidths({}, [{ id: 'a', minWidth: 60.5, size: undefined }, ...shown.slice(1)], 'b', 240),
+    ).toEqual({ a: 61, b: 240, c: 311 });
+  });
+
+  it('is a new record, and keeps the widths of columns that are not shown', () => {
+    const widths = { z: 50 };
+    const frozen = freezeWidths(widths, shown, 'a', 110);
+    expect(frozen).not.toBe(widths);
+    expect(frozen.z).toBe(50);
+    expect(widths).toEqual({ z: 50 });
+  });
+});

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1af85a1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/internal/auto-scroll.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,159 @@
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { createAutoScroll } from './auto-scroll';
+
+// A frame clock the test drives by hand, and an element whose box is 100..500 across and 50..250
+// down, so each case says where the pointer is and how many frames have passed.
+
+const queue = new Map<number, FrameRequestCallback>();
+let next = 1;
+const runFrame = () => {
+  const callbacks = [...queue.values()];
+  queue.clear();
+  for (const callback of callbacks) callback(0);
+};
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  queue.clear();
+  next = 1;
+  vi.stubGlobal('requestAnimationFrame', (callback: FrameRequestCallback) => {
+    queue.set(next, callback);
+    return next++;
+  });
+  vi.stubGlobal('cancelAnimationFrame', (id: number) => {
+    queue.delete(id);
+  });
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+});
+
+function box() {
+  const element = document.createElement('div');
+  element.getBoundingClientRect = () =>
+    ({ left: 100, right: 500, top: 50, bottom: 250, width: 400, height: 200 }) as DOMRect;
+  element.scrollLeft = 200;
+  element.scrollTop = 200;
+  return element;
+}
+
+describe('createAutoScroll', () => {
+  it('scrolls nothing while the pointer is 40px or more from every edge', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    const scroll = createAutoScroll(element, { axis: 'both' });
+    scroll.update(300, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(200);
+    expect(element.scrollTop).toBe(200);
+    expect(queue.size).toBe(0);
+    scroll.update(140, 90);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(200);
+    expect(element.scrollTop).toBe(200);
+  });
+
+  it('scrolls towards an edge by a share of 20px a frame that grows as the pointer nears it', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    const scroll = createAutoScroll(element, { axis: 'x' });
+    // 20px from the left edge: half of the zone, so half the speed, 10px.
+    scroll.update(120, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(190);
+    // 10px from the right edge: three quarters, 15px.
+    scroll.update(490, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(205);
+    scroll.stop();
+  });
+
+  it('scrolls 20px a frame at the edge and beyond it', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    const scroll = createAutoScroll(element, { axis: 'x' });
+    scroll.update(100, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(180);
+    scroll.update(-300, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(160);
+    scroll.update(500, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(180);
+    scroll.update(900, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(200);
+    scroll.stop();
+  });
+
+  it('keeps scrolling a frame at a time under a pointer that does not move', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    const scroll = createAutoScroll(element, { axis: 'x' });
+    scroll.update(500, 150);
+    runFrame();
+    runFrame();
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(260);
+    scroll.stop();
+  });
+
+  it('scrolls on the axis it is given and leaves the other', () => {
+    const horizontal = box();
+    createAutoScroll(horizontal, { axis: 'x' }).update(500, 250);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(horizontal.scrollLeft).toBe(220);
+    expect(horizontal.scrollTop).toBe(200);
+
+    const vertical = box();
+    createAutoScroll(vertical, { axis: 'y' }).update(500, 250);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(vertical.scrollLeft).toBe(200);
+    expect(vertical.scrollTop).toBe(220);
+
+    const both = box();
+    createAutoScroll(both, { axis: 'both' }).update(100, 50);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(both.scrollLeft).toBe(180);
+    expect(both.scrollTop).toBe(180);
+  });
+
+  it('scrolls on both axes when it is not told', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    createAutoScroll(element).update(500, 250);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(220);
+    expect(element.scrollTop).toBe(220);
+  });
+
+  it('ends the loop when the pointer leaves the zones', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    const scroll = createAutoScroll(element, { axis: 'x' });
+    scroll.update(500, 150);
+    expect(queue.size).toBe(1);
+    runFrame();
+    scroll.update(300, 150);
+    expect(queue.size).toBe(0);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(220);
+  });
+
+  it('asks for one frame at a time, however often it is told where the pointer is', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    const scroll = createAutoScroll(element, { axis: 'x' });
+    scroll.update(500, 150);
+    scroll.update(499, 150);
+    scroll.update(498, 150);
+    expect(queue.size).toBe(1);
+    scroll.stop();
+  });
+
+  it('stops: the frame it asked for is cancelled and nothing scrolls after', () => {
+    const element = box();
+    const scroll = createAutoScroll(element, { axis: 'x' });
+    scroll.update(500, 150);
+    expect(queue.size).toBe(1);
+    scroll.stop();
+    expect(queue.size).toBe(0);
+    runFrame();
+    expect(element.scrollLeft).toBe(200);
+    // Told again after it stopped, it stays stopped until it is given a new pointer.
+    scroll.stop();
+  });
+});
```

@@ -324,7 +324,7 @@ Chủ dự án chọn một phương án cho mỗi câu, nên `Kbd`, `DialogCont
 
 - **Cột có `width`:** đúng số đó; grid không có cột co giãn nào thì bảng có thêm một **cột đệm** ở cuối: `<col>` không có `width`, và mỗi hàng một ô rỗng (`th` ở hàng tiêu đề; `td` ở dòng dữ liệu, dòng skeleton; `colspan` của dòng trống và hàng đệm của cuộn ảo tính cả nó) có `aria-hidden="true"`, không `tabindex`, lớp `flg-data-grid-filler` cùng lớp ô của `Table`, không padding. Bảng rộng bằng tổng các cột (`width` px) và ít nhất bằng khung (`min-width: 100%`), nên cột đệm lấy `max(0, bề rộng khung − tổng)` bằng CSS, không cần số đo (HTML từ server như nhau); không dùng `width: 100%` với `min-width` bằng tổng, vì Firefox không cho bảng `width: 100%` bề rộng nội tại nào, nên grid trong một hộp co theo nội dung (căn giữa bằng flex, `fit-content`) đóng lại còn 0px, khung hẹp hơn tổng thì vẫn cuộn ngang, và mọi cột thật giữ đúng độ rộng của nó (không có cột đệm thì trình duyệt chia phần thừa theo tỉ lệ cho mọi cột, và `width` thành tỉ lệ). Cột đệm không phải cột của grid: không có trong các cột đã chuẩn hoá, mũi tên, `Home`/`End`, `mod+End` không tới nó (`End` tới cột thật cuối), không bao giờ là ô hoạt động; con trỏ trên nó là trên dòng của nó (dòng vẫn hover), còn lần nhấn trên nó bị huỷ `mousedown` (focus ở nguyên chỗ, khung với `tabindex="-1"` không lấy nó) và không làm gì: không đổi ô hoạt động, không chọn dòng, nhấn đúp không gọi `onRowActivate` (vòng sửa sau review lại); nhưng nó mang những gì dòng vẽ trên bề rộng của nó (vạch của `lined`, nền hover và chọn, sọc và góc bo phải của `striped`, dải tiêu đề dính), nên mỗi dòng là một dải tới mép khung. Có cột co giãn thì không có cột đệm (phát hiện khi review cuối Plan B; chủ dự án chọn phương án E ngày 2026-11-17). **Khi có vùng ghim phải, cột đệm (`<col>` và ô của nó ở tiêu đề, dòng dữ liệu, dòng skeleton) nằm trước vùng ấy** (phát hiện khi lập Plan C; Claude chốt OQ 3): vùng phải kết thúc dòng đúng ở mép khung, còn cột đệm vẫn lấy phần dư ở giữa; không có vùng phải thì nó ở cuối như trước. Vì cột đệm không còn luôn là ô cuối, `grid-dom.ts` có `cellsOf(row)` (các ô của dòng không kể cột đệm) và bàn phím (`cellAt`, `activate`) đi qua nó, không qua `cellIndex` hay `cells[i]`; `colspan` của dòng trống và hàng đệm không đổi. Cột đệm chỉ có trong DOM khi khung đủ chỗ cho nó mang đầu cuối của dòng: khi khung chưa được đo (server, lần render đầu ở client, jsdom, grid bị ẩn: khung đo ra 0 không tính là đo) hoặc khi phần dư (bề rộng khung trừ thanh cuộn và padding, trừ tổng các cột) ít nhất là `max(1, độ bo)`; độ bo là `border-top-right-radius` đã tính (px) của ô cuối của dòng đầu tiên trong `.flg-table-body` của khung, không có dòng như thế hay giá trị không đọc được thì là 0. Vậy `lined` và `minimal` (độ bo 0) có cột đệm từ 1px dư, `striped` cần đủ độ bo (8px với token mặc định). Thiếu chỗ thì không có cột đệm: bảng rộng đúng tổng các cột (`width` và `min-width` bằng tổng, vì `width: 100%` của `Table` sẽ chia phần dư cho các cột), dòng `striped` kết thúc bo tròn cách mép khung vài px như trước phương án E, và mọi `colspan` (dòng trống, hàng đệm) không tính nó. Lý do: cột đệm 0px hay 2px vẫn là `:last-child` của dòng, nên lấy mất các quy tắc cho đầu cuối dòng của `Table` (góc bo phải của `striped`, cạnh phải của khung 2px quanh dòng chọn khi `prefers-contrast: more`). Grid đo khung bằng một `ResizeObserver` cả khi mọi cột có `width`, đọc lại độ bo khi `variant` hoặc `density` đổi và khi các dòng thay chỗ lời của grid rỗng (lời ấy không phải dòng để đọc), khung đo ra 0 thì giữ kết quả cũ. Ở client, effect bố cục quyết định trước lần vẽ đầu, nên không chớp; một trang hydrate thì những khung hình trước khi hydrate là HTML của server, có cột đệm, rồi lần commit của hydrate bỏ nó trước lần vẽ kế tiếp (phát hiện khi soát ảnh chuẩn PR #42). **Cột không có `width`** co giãn: chia đều phần còn lại của bề rộng khung (đo bằng `ResizeObserver`), không dưới `minWidth` (mặc định 60px). Khi có cột co giãn, bảng rộng `max(bề rộng khung, tổng các cột)` (phát hiện khi review cuối Plan B: câu này chỉ đúng khi có cột co giãn); rộng hơn khung thì khung cuộn ngang.
 - **Trước khi đo** (HTML từ server, lần render hydrate): cột co giãn là `<col>` không có `width`, bảng `width: 100%` và `min-width` bằng tổng các độ rộng cố định cộng `minWidth` của cột co giãn; CSS tự chia. Sau khi đo, mọi cột có px chính xác (cột ghim cần px để tính vị trí dính). Cột ghim không có `width` tính `minWidth` của nó cho đến khi khung được đo (phát hiện khi lập Plan C): đó là cận dưới, nên một ô không bao giờ dính ở bên phải chỗ nó nằm trong HTML của server; sau khi đo thì là px đã đo.
-- **Đổi độ rộng kiểu "widget"** (bản quyết định): lần kéo đầu ghi độ rộng px hiện tại của **mọi** cột co giãn vào `columnLayout.widths`, nên kéo một cột chỉ làm bảng rộng ra hay hẹp lại, không lấy chỗ của cột bên cạnh. Hệ quả: sau đó các cột không co giãn theo cửa sổ nữa (như DevExtreme); "Tự vừa" hay xoá `widths` (lưu trạng thái) trả lại (Claude chốt).
+- **Đổi độ rộng kiểu "widget"** (bản quyết định): lần kéo đầu ghi độ rộng px hiện tại của **mọi** cột co giãn vào `columnLayout.widths`, nên kéo một cột chỉ làm bảng rộng ra hay hẹp lại, không lấy chỗ của cột bên cạnh. Hệ quả: sau đó các cột không co giãn theo cửa sổ nữa (như DevExtreme); chỉ xoá `widths` (lưu trạng thái) mới trả lại; "Tự vừa" (bấm đúp tay nắm, mục của menu cột) đặt một độ rộng đã đo, nên không trả cột về co giãn (Claude chốt OQ 6; phát hiện khi lập Plan C).

 #### DataGrid: thao tác cột (C1)
 
-- **Tay nắm đổi độ rộng** (`.flg-data-grid-resizer`, trong ô tiêu đề có `allowResizing`): tuyệt đối, `z-index: 3`, `top: 0; bottom: 0; right: -5px`, rộng 10px, `flex` căn giữa, `cursor: col-resize`, `touch-action: none`; ở `@media (pointer: coarse)`: `right: -12px`, rộng 24px (WCAG 2.5.8). `::before`: 1×14px, nền `--flg-column-resize-line` (vạch mảnh luôn có). Hover và đang kéo: `::before` 3px × 100%, bo 2px, `--flg-accent-solid`.
-- **Đang kéo độ rộng:** cột đổi rộng ngay theo con trỏ (bản quyết định); đường dẫn `.flg-data-grid-resize-guide` tuyệt đối trong khung, rộng 2px, `--flg-accent-solid`, từ mép dưới của `<thead>` tới đáy phần thấy được của khung, thẳng tâm tay nắm; nhãn `.flg-data-grid-width-pill` (`aria-hidden`, `labels.columnWidth(px)`, "180 px"): đỉnh cách mép dưới của tiêu đề 10px, mép phải cách đường dẫn 6px về bên trái, padding `2px 8px`, viền 1px `--flg-accent-solid`, bo `--flg-radius-full`, nền `--flg-glass-tint-solid`, chữ `--flg-text` đậm `--flg-weight-semibold` `--flg-text-2xs`/1.3, `tabular-nums`, không xuống dòng. `cursor: col-resize` trên cả trang trong lúc kéo.
+- **Tay nắm đổi độ rộng** (`.flg-data-grid-resizer`, trong ô tiêu đề có `allowResizing`): tuyệt đối, `z-index: 1` (phát hiện khi lập Plan C, Claude chốt OQ 7: trên tiêu đề kế bên, dưới tiêu đề ghim, là 3 trong ngữ cảnh xếp chồng của `<thead>`; ô tiêu đề có `position: relative`), `top: 0; bottom: 0; right: -5px`, rộng 10px, `flex` căn giữa, `cursor: col-resize`, `touch-action: none`; ở `@media (pointer: coarse)`: `right: -12px`, rộng 24px (WCAG 2.5.8). `::before`: 1×14px, nền `--flg-column-resize-line` (vạch mảnh luôn có). Hover (chỉ ở `(hover: hover)`) và đang kéo (`data-dragging` trên tay nắm, grid ghi trực tiếp): `::before` 3px × 100%, bo 2px, `--flg-accent-solid`. Tiêu đề cuối hàng (không có cột đệm sau nó) có tay nắm nằm trong ô (`right: 0`) và không vẽ vạch lúc nghỉ: tay nắm ngoài bảng làm khung cuộn rộng thêm 5px, và vạch ở mép khung bị cắt nửa (phát hiện khi lập Plan C).
+- **Đang kéo độ rộng:** cột đổi rộng ngay theo con trỏ (bản quyết định); đường dẫn `.flg-data-grid-resize-guide` tuyệt đối trong `.flg-data-grid-main` (phát hiện khi lập Plan C: không trong khung, vì khung cuộn nó theo dòng; grid đặt `left`, `top`, `height` bằng số đo DOM sau mỗi lần commit của lần kéo), rộng 2px, `--flg-accent-solid`, từ mép dưới của tay nắm (cao hơn mép dưới của `<thead>` 1px: viền dưới của ô tiêu đề, như mockup; phát hiện khi lập Plan C) tới đáy phần thấy được của khung, thẳng tâm tay nắm; nhãn `.flg-data-grid-width-pill` (`aria-hidden`, `labels.columnWidth(px)`, "180 px"): đỉnh cách mép dưới của tay nắm 10px, mép phải cách tâm đường dẫn 6px về bên trái, padding `2px 8px`, viền 1px `--flg-accent-solid`, bo `--flg-radius-full`, nền `--flg-glass-tint-solid`, chữ `--flg-text` đậm `--flg-weight-semibold` `--flg-text-2xs`/1.3, `tabular-nums`, không xuống dòng. `cursor: col-resize` trên cả trang trong lúc kéo.
 - **Kéo cột:** ô tiêu đề và mọi ô của cột gốc `opacity: .35`. Bóng là chip `.flg-surface.flg-data-grid-drag-chip` trong top layer (`popover="manual"`, `pointer-events: none`), cách con trỏ 16px sang phải và 16px xuống (theo hình): `inline-flex`, căn giữa, khoảng cách 4px, padding `5px 11px 5px 7px`, bo `--flg-radius-full`, chữ `--flg-text` đậm `--flg-weight-semibold` `--flg-text-xs`/1.3, `GripVerticalIcon` 13px `--flg-text-muted` trước chữ. Chỗ thả: `.flg-data-grid-drop-line` tuyệt đối trong khung, rộng 3px, cao hết phần thấy được của khung, `--flg-accent-solid`, tâm lệch −0.5px khỏi ranh giới hai cột (`left: ranh giới − 2px`); `::before` là chấm 7×7px tròn `--flg-accent-solid` ở đỉnh, `left: -2px`. `cursor: grabbing`.

+## Resizing columns
+
+A column that can be resized has a handle on the right edge of its title: a thin line between the
+titles that becomes a bar of 3px in the accent under the pointer. `allowResizing` is the default of
+every column (`true`), and a column's own `allowResizing` wins; the column of boxes has no handle.
+The handle is for a pointer: it is hidden from a screen reader and is no stop of Tab, so the keys
+below are the way for everyone else.
+
+- **Drag it.** A press that moves 4px or more is a drag, with a mouse, a pen or a finger (the
+  handle is 24px wide for a finger, and takes no scroll from it). The column is as wide as the
+  pointer says, at least its `minWidth` (60 when left out) and at most 2000px, and it follows the
+  frame when it scrolls sideways: a pointer held within 40px of the frame's edge scrolls the frame,
+  faster the closer it is, and the column goes on growing. A line runs down the grid from the
+  handle, and a label says the width (`labels.columnWidth`). The cursor is `col-resize` over the
+  whole page until the pointer is let go. A drag is not a click: the click that its release makes
+  is not delivered, so the column is not sorted. <Kbd keys="esc" /> puts the column back as it was.
+- **One change, at the release.** While the pointer moves, the widths live in the grid and only
+  the table is drawn again: no row, no title and no toolbar. `onColumnLayoutChange` is called once,
+  at the release, with the layout as shown (and then `onStateChange(state, 'columnLayout')`); a drag
+  that is cancelled, or that ends at the width it began with, calls nothing. A grid that is
+  controlled and keeps its `columnLayout` sees the column go back at the release.
+- **Columns without a width are frozen.** The first resize of a grid whose columns share the frame
+  (the ones with no `width`) writes the width each has at that moment into `columnLayout.widths`,
+  with the new width of the column, so a drag makes the table wider or narrower and never takes the
+  room of a neighbour. From then on the columns do not follow the width of the window. Only a
+  layout with no `widths` for them makes them flexible again; "fit" below sets a width and does not.
+  A grid whose columns all have a width has the filler column (see Widths) at the end of its rows
+  when the frame is wider than the columns.
+- **Fit.** A double press on the handle gives the column the width that its title and the cells it
+  has drawn need, at most 600px and at least `minWidth`. It reads the widths from the page and
+  changes nothing to do it, so the frame does not scroll. Only the rows that are drawn count: a
+  page, or the window of a virtual grid, and not the rows that are not; a column with none fits its
+  title. A custom `cell` that stretches to the width of its cell (a block, a flex container) is
+  measured at that width, so it does not fit narrower than it is. It is one change of the layout,
+  and the clicks of the double press do nothing else.
+- **Keys.** <Kbd keys="alt+shift+left" /> and <Kbd keys="alt+shift+right" /> on the title of a
+  column make it 10px narrower or wider, within the same limits, and the frozen widths of the others
+  come with the first press. Each press is one change of the layout. The new width is said, once,
+  half a second after the last press (`labels.announceResized`), and after a fit. The keys are
+  cancelled on the title of every data column, also on one that cannot be resized.
+
+```tsx
+<DataGrid
+  data={orders}
+  rowKey="id"
+  columns={[
+    { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', width: 104, allowResizing: false },
+    { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', minWidth: 120 },
+    { field: 'total', caption: 'Total', dataType: 'number', width: 160 },
+  ]}
+  columnLayout={layout}
+  onColumnLayoutChange={setLayout}
+/>
+```
+
+The last title of a row has its handle inside the cell, so that it does not widen what the frame
+scrolls, and draws no line until the pointer is over it. In forced colours the line is the text
+colour and the bar is `Highlight`; with more contrast the line is solid.
+
+### Touch
+
+| Action          | Pointer (mouse, pen)               | Touch                                             | Without dragging                                             |
+| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
+| Resize a column | Drag the handle; double press fits | Drag the handle (24px wide, `touch-action: none`) | <Kbd keys="alt+shift+left" /> <Kbd keys="alt+shift+right" /> |
+

+
+/** The widest a column gets from "fit to its content", in pixels (spec phase 6 §6.3). */
+export const MAX_FIT_WIDTH = 600;
+
+/**
+ * A width as a drag, a key or a fit leaves it: in whole pixels, not under the least width of the
+ * column (a least width with a fraction counts as the next whole pixel, as `resolveWidths` counts
+ * it) and not over `MAX_COLUMN_WIDTH`. A width that is no number is the least width. A column whose
+ * least width is over the greatest keeps its least.
+ */
+export function clampWidth(width: number, minWidth: number): number {
+  const least = Math.ceil(minWidth);
+  return isNumber(width) ? Math.max(least, Math.min(MAX_COLUMN_WIDTH, Math.round(width))) : least;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The width a column gets from "fit to its content": the widest of what the title and the drawn
+ * cells need, in whole pixels, held to the least width of the column and to `MAX_FIT_WIDTH` (the
+ * least width wins where it is the greater). Nothing to measure is the least width.
+ */
+export function autoFitWidth(measures: readonly number[], minWidth: number): number {
+  const least = Math.ceil(minWidth);
+  return Math.max(least, Math.min(MAX_FIT_WIDTH, Math.ceil(Math.max(...measures))));
+}
+
+/**
+ * The widths of a layout when a column is resized the first time (spec phase 6 §3.7, the widget
+ * freeze): every shown column that has no width in `widths` gets the one it has now, `size` (its
+ * least width when it was not measured), and `id` gets `width`. So a drag or a key makes the table
+ * wider or narrower and never takes the room of a neighbour. A width the layout has is kept, and so
+ * is that of a column that is not shown. A new record.
+ */
+export function freezeWidths(
+  widths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>,
+  columns: readonly { id: string; minWidth: number; size: number | undefined }[],
+  id: string,
+  width: number,
+): Record<string, number> {
+  const frozen: Record<string, number> = { ...widths };
+  for (const column of columns) {
+    if (frozen[column.id] === undefined) {
+      frozen[column.id] = clampWidth(column.size ?? 0, column.minWidth);
+    }
+  }
+  frozen[id] = width;
+  return frozen;
+}
+
+/** What a press of `Alt+Shift+←` or `Alt+Shift+→` on a title changes the width of its column by, in pixels. */
+export const RESIZE_KEY_STEP = 10;

+/**

+ * of the boxes in it even where the cell cuts them off with an ellipsis, and scaled back by how much a
+ * transform makes the cell's box differ from its layout size, so a grid in a panel that scales in

+function widthOfCell(cell: HTMLTableCellElement): number {

+  const content = range.getBoundingClientRect().width * scale;

+ * What a title needs to show its words whole: the room its content takes, which is the sum of its
+ * parts and the gaps between them, plus the part of each title text that is cut off (its
+ * `scrollWidth` beyond its `clientWidth`), plus what the cell has around the content. Read from sizes
+ * in layout pixels, which a transform does not change.
+ */
+function widthOfTitle(title: HTMLTableCellElement): number {
+  const content = title.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-head-content');
+  if (!content) return widthOfCell(title);
+  const parts = Array.from(content.children, (part) => (part as HTMLElement).offsetWidth);
+  const gap = lengthOf(getComputedStyle(content).columnGap);
+  const cut = Array.from(
+    content.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-head-title'),
+    (text) => Math.max(0, text.scrollWidth - text.clientWidth),
+  );
+  const natural =
+    parts.reduce((sum, part) => sum + part, 0) +
+    gap * Math.max(0, parts.length - 1) +
+    cut.reduce((sum, part) => sum + part, 0);
+  return natural + (title.offsetWidth - content.offsetWidth);
+}
+
+/**
+ * What the column at `index` (among the cells of a row, the filler column not counted) needs to show
+ * everything in it: one measure for its title and one for each of its cells that is drawn (a virtual
+ * grid draws a window, a grid with no rows none). `autoFitWidth` takes the greatest.
+ */
+export function measureColumn(table: HTMLTableElement, index: number): number[] {
+  const measures: number[] = [];
+  const title = table.tHead?.rows[0] ? cellsOf(table.tHead.rows[0])[index] : undefined;
+  if (title) measures.push(widthOfTitle(title));
+  for (const row of dataRows(table)) {
+    const cell = cellsOf(row)[index];
+    if (cell) measures.push(widthOfCell(cell));
+  }
+  return measures;
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-resize.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-resize.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..3542e1a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-column-resize.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,240 @@
+import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import type { PointerEvent as ReactPointerEvent, RefObject } from 'react';
+import { createAutoScroll } from '../../../internal/auto-scroll';
+import type { AutoScroll } from '../../../internal/auto-scroll';
+import { usePointerDrag } from '../../../internal/use-pointer-drag';
+import { useWriteOnCommit } from '../../../internal/use-write-on-commit';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import { autoFitWidth, clampWidth, freezeWidths } from '../engine/layout';
+import { markDragCursor, measureColumn } from '../grid-dom';
+import type { DataGridColumnLayout, DataGridLabels } from '../types';
+import type { LiveWidthsStore } from './use-live-widths';
+
+/** How long after the last key the new width is said, so a held key is said once. */
+const ANNOUNCE_DELAY = 500;
+
+export interface ColumnResizeOptions<TRow> {
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
+  tableRef: RefObject<HTMLTableElement | null>;
+  /** The shown columns, the column of boxes first when there is one. */
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  /** The width in pixels each of `columns` has now, once known: `undefined` before the frame is measured. */
+  sizes: readonly (number | undefined)[];
+  /** The layout as shown. */
+  layout: DataGridColumnLayout;
+  setColumnLayout: (next: DataGridColumnLayout) => void;
+  store: LiveWidthsStore;
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  /** Says a text through the grid's live region; `delay` joins the calls made within it, and says the last. */
+  announce: (text: string, options?: { delay?: number }) => void;
+}
+
+export interface ColumnResize {
+  /** The press on the handle of the column `columnId`: the start of a drag. */
+  onPointerDown: (event: ReactPointerEvent<HTMLElement>, columnId: string) => void;
+  /** The double press on that handle: fits the column to its content. */
+  onDoubleClick: (columnId: string) => void;
+  /** Changes the width of a column by `delta` pixels, held to its limits (the keys). */
+  resizeBy: (columnId: string, delta: number) => void;
+  /** Gives a column the width its title and its drawn cells need (the double press, the menu). */
+  fit: (columnId: string) => void;
+}
+
+/** A drag from its first move to its end. */
+interface Session {
+  id: string;
+  handle: HTMLElement;
+  frame: HTMLElement;
+  doc: Document;
+  /** The width of the column when the press began, and its least. */
+  start: number;
+  minWidth: number;
+  /** Where the frame was scrolled then, so that a scroll under a still pointer widens the column. */
+  scrollStart: number;
+  /** The widths of every shown column, with the flexible ones frozen at what they measured. */
+  frozen: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
+  /** How far the pointer is from where it was pressed, and the widths now. */
+  dx: number;
+  widths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
+  autoScroll: AutoScroll;
+  onScroll: () => void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Resizing the columns (spec phase 6 §3.7, §3.8, §6.3): a drag of the handle on the right edge of a
+ * title, the double press on it, and the keys. One `usePointerDrag` serves the whole heading.
+ *
+ * While a drag is in flight, the widths are written into the live store, which only the table and
+ * the guide read: no row, no title and no toolbar is drawn for a move. The width is where the
+ * pointer is, plus how far the frame has scrolled since the press, so a frame that scrolls under a
+ * pointer at its edge (`createAutoScroll`) widens the column too. The first resize of a grid with
+ * flexible columns freezes them at the width they measured (the widget freeze), so a drag makes the
+ * table wider or narrower and never takes the room of a neighbour. The layout is changed once, at
+ * the release; Escape, `pointercancel` and a lost capture only take the live widths away. What the
+ * drag set on the page (the cursor mark, the attribute on the handle, the scroll listener, the
+ * auto-scroll) is taken off on each of those ends and when the grid goes in the middle of one.
+ *
+ * Everything the handlers read comes from the latest commit, so they are the same functions for as
+ * long as the grid lives.
+ */
+export function useColumnResize<TRow>(options: ColumnResizeOptions<TRow>): ColumnResize {
+  const latest = useRef(options);
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    latest.current = options;
+  });
+  const pressed = useRef<{ id: string; handle: HTMLElement } | null>(null);
+  const session = useRef<Session | null>(null);
+
+  /** The shown data columns with the width each has now, for the freeze. */
+  const shown = useCallback(() => {
+    const { columns, sizes } = latest.current;
+    return columns.flatMap((column, index) =>
+      column.service === undefined
+        ? [{ id: column.id, minWidth: column.minWidth, size: sizes[index] }]
+        : [],
+    );
+  }, []);
+
+  /** The column of `id` if it can be resized, with its place among the shown columns. */
+  const resizable = useCallback((id: string) => {
+    const index = latest.current.columns.findIndex((column) => column.id === id);
+    const column = latest.current.columns[index];
+    return column && column.service === undefined && column.allowResizing
+      ? { column, index }
+      : undefined;
+  }, []);
+
+  const widthNow = useCallback((index: number) => {
+    const { columns, sizes, layout } = latest.current;
+    const column = columns[index]!;
+    return sizes[index] ?? layout.widths[column.id] ?? column.minWidth;
+  }, []);
+
+  // Where the pointer is now says a width; the frame's scroll since the press adds to it.
+  const apply = useCallback((current: Session, dx: number) => {
+    current.dx = dx;
+    const moved = current.frame.scrollLeft - current.scrollStart;
+    current.widths = {
+      ...current.frozen,
+      [current.id]: clampWidth(current.start + dx + moved, current.minWidth),
+    };
+    latest.current.store.set({ id: current.id, handle: current.handle, widths: current.widths });
+  }, []);
+
+  // Everything a drag set, taken off: the one place that does it, for each way a drag ends.
+  const settle = useCallback((current: Session) => {
+    current.autoScroll.stop();
+    current.frame.removeEventListener('scroll', current.onScroll);
+    markDragCursor(current.doc, null);
+    current.handle.removeAttribute('data-dragging');
+  }, []);
+
+  const finish = useCallback(
+    (commit: boolean) => {
+      const current = session.current;
+      if (!current) return;
+      session.current = null;
+      settle(current);
+      const { layout, setColumnLayout, store } = latest.current;
+      if (commit) {
+        setColumnLayout({ ...layout, widths: { ...layout.widths, ...current.widths } });
+      }
+      // After the layout, so a column does not go back to its old width for a frame between the two.
+      store.set(null);
+    },
+    [settle],
+  );
+
+  const drag = usePointerDrag({
+    onStart: () => {
+      const press = pressed.current;
+      const found = press && resizable(press.id);
+      const frame = latest.current.frameRef.current;
+      if (!press || !found || !frame) return;
+      const start = widthNow(found.index);
+      const doc = frame.ownerDocument;
+      const next: Session = {
+        id: press.id,
+        handle: press.handle,
+        frame,
+        doc,
+        start,
+        minWidth: found.column.minWidth,
+        scrollStart: frame.scrollLeft,
+        frozen: freezeWidths(latest.current.layout.widths, shown(), press.id, start),
+        dx: 0,
+        widths: {},
+        autoScroll: createAutoScroll(frame, { axis: 'x' }),
+        onScroll: () => apply(next, next.dx),
+      };
+      session.current = next;
+      frame.addEventListener('scroll', next.onScroll, { passive: true });
+      press.handle.setAttribute('data-dragging', '');
+      markDragCursor(doc, 'col-resize');
+    },
+    onMove: ({ dx, x, y }) => {
+      const current = session.current;
+      if (!current) return;
+      apply(current, dx);
+      current.autoScroll.update(x, y);
+    },
+    onEnd: () => finish(true),
+    onCancel: () => finish(false),
+  });
+
+  useEffect(
+    () => () => {
+      const current = session.current;
+      session.current = null;
+      if (current) settle(current);
+    },
+    [settle],
+  );
+
+  const setWidth = useCallback(
+    (id: string, caption: string, width: number) => {
+      const { layout, setColumnLayout, labels, announce } = latest.current;
+      setColumnLayout({ ...layout, widths: freezeWidths(layout.widths, shown(), id, width) });
+      announce(labels.announceResized(caption, width), { delay: ANNOUNCE_DELAY });
+    },
+    [shown],
+  );
+
+  const resizeBy = useCallback(
+    (id: string, delta: number) => {
+      const found = resizable(id);
+      if (!found) return;
+      const now = widthNow(found.index);
+      const width = clampWidth(now + delta, found.column.minWidth);
+      if (width !== now) setWidth(id, found.column.caption, width);
+    },
+    [resizable, widthNow, setWidth],
+  );
+
+  const fit = useCallback(
+    (id: string) => {
+      const found = resizable(id);
+      const table = latest.current.tableRef.current;
+      if (!found || !table) return;
+      const width = autoFitWidth(measureColumn(table, found.index), found.column.minWidth);
+      if (width !== widthNow(found.index)) setWidth(id, found.column.caption, width);
+    },
+    [resizable, widthNow, setWidth],
+  );
+
+  // The hook's handler is the same function for as long as the grid lives, and so is what this returns:
+  // it is in the grid's context, which draws every row when it changes.
+  const { onPointerDown: startDrag } = drag;
+  return useMemo(
+    () => ({
+      onPointerDown: (event, columnId) => {
+        pressed.current = { id: columnId, handle: event.currentTarget };
+        startDrag(event);
+      },
+      onDoubleClick: fit,
+      resizeBy,
+      fit,
+    }),
+    [startDrag, fit, resizeBy],
+  );
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-live-widths.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-live-widths.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..00ff290
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-live-widths.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
+
+/** What a column resize in flight says to the table: the width of every column, for as long as it lasts. */
+export interface LiveWidths {
+  /** The id of the column that is dragged. */
+  readonly id: string;
+  /** The handle that is pressed, which the guide stands on. */
+  readonly handle: HTMLElement;
+  /**
+   * The width of every shown column in pixels: the ones the layout has and the ones the first resize
+   * freezes, and the dragged column's own. Each snapshot is a new object, also when no width changed
+   * (the frame scrolled under a still pointer), so what reads it measures again.
+   */
+  readonly widths: Readonly<Record<string, number>>;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The widths of a drag, apart from what the rows read: the table (`<col>`, its width, the offsets of
+ * the pinned columns) and the guide read them, and nothing else does, so a move of the pointer draws
+ * no row, no title and no toolbar (spec phase 6 §3.7, option b of the owner's review of PR #42).
+ * `null` while no column is dragged.
+ */
+export interface LiveWidthsStore {
+  get(): LiveWidths | null;
+  set(next: LiveWidths | null): void;
+  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
+}
+
+/** One store for one grid. */
+export function createLiveWidths(): LiveWidthsStore {
+  let current: LiveWidths | null = null;
+  const listeners = new Set<() => void>();
+  return {
+    get: () => current,
+    set(next) {
+      current = next;
+      for (const listener of [...listeners]) listener();
+    },
+    subscribe(listener) {
+      listeners.add(listener);
+      return () => void listeners.delete(listener);
+    },
+  };
+}
+
+const NONE = () => null;
+
+/** The drag in flight, `null` when there is none (and on the server). */
+export function useLiveWidths(store: LiveWidthsStore): LiveWidths | null {
+  return useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, store.get, NONE);
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/ResizeGuide.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/ResizeGuide.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..757f560
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/ResizeGuide.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+import { useRef } from 'react';
+import type { RefObject } from 'react';
+import { useIsoLayoutEffect } from '../../../internal/use-iso-layout-effect';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+import { useLiveWidths } from '../hooks/use-live-widths';
+import type { LiveWidthsStore } from '../hooks/use-live-widths';
+
+/**
+ * The line down the grid from the handle that is dragged, and the label that says the width (spec
+ * phase 6 §4.3 C1 "Đang kéo độ rộng"). One per grid, and only while a column is dragged: it is in
+ * `.flg-data-grid-main`, which is the box the loading layer is placed against too, and not in the
+ * frame, whose content it would scroll with. It reads the live widths and nothing the rows read, so
+ * a move of the pointer draws only this and the table.
+ *
+ * Where it stands is read from the DOM after each commit of a drag, which is after the table has
+ * taken the new width: the middle of the handle, from the bottom of the handle (the heading's own
+ * border, a pixel above the bottom of the heading, is under it, as in the mockup) to the bottom of
+ * what the frame shows (the frame's scrollbar is not part of it). It is hidden while the handle is
+ * outside what the frame shows (the frame scrolls under a pointer at its edge). Sizes are in layout
+ * pixels, scaled back by the one the grid is drawn at, so a grid in a panel that scales in measures
+ * right. It is for the eye alone: it takes no pointer and is hidden from a screen reader, which hears
+ * the width from the keys' announcement.
+ */
+export function ResizeGuide({
+  live,
+  frameRef,
+}: {
+  live: LiveWidthsStore;
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
+}) {
+  const { labels } = useGridContext();
+  const dragged = useLiveWidths(live);
+  const guide = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
+
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const line = guide.current;
+    const main = line?.parentElement;
+    const frame = frameRef.current;
+    if (!dragged || !line || !main || !frame) return;
+    const box = main.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const scale = box.width > 0 ? main.offsetWidth / box.width : 1;
+    const handle = dragged.handle.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const middle = (handle.left + handle.right) / 2;
+    const top = handle.bottom;
+    const area = frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const bottom = area.top + frame.clientTop + frame.clientHeight;
+    const left = area.left + frame.clientLeft;
+    line.style.left = `${(middle - box.left) * scale - 1}px`;
+    line.style.top = `${(top - box.top) * scale}px`;
+    line.style.height = `${Math.max(0, (bottom - top) * scale)}px`;
+    line.style.visibility = middle < left || middle > left + frame.clientWidth ? 'hidden' : '';
+  }, [dragged, frameRef]);
+
+  if (!dragged) return null;
+  return (
+    <div ref={guide} className="flg-data-grid-resize-guide" aria-hidden="true">
+      <span className="flg-data-grid-width-pill">
+        {labels.columnWidth(dragged.widths[dragged.id] ?? 0)}
+      </span>
+    </div>
+  );
+}

diff --git a/src/internal/auto-scroll.ts b/src/internal/auto-scroll.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bfe3c6c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/internal/auto-scroll.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+import { clamp } from './number';
+
+/** How close to an edge of the element, in pixels, the pointer starts to scroll it. */
+const ZONE = 40;
+/** The most it scrolls in a frame, at the edge and beyond it. */
+const MAX_STEP = 20;
+
+export interface AutoScrollOptions {
+  /** The directions it scrolls in; `'both'` when left out. */
+  axis?: 'x' | 'y' | 'both';
+}
+
+export interface AutoScroll {
+  /** Tells it where the pointer is, in the client coordinates of the viewport. */
+  update(x: number, y: number): void;
+  /** Ends the loop; what `update` says after it starts it again. */
+  stop(): void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * How far to scroll in a frame for a pointer at `position` along an axis whose element runs from
+ * `start` to `end`: 0 while it is `ZONE` or more from both edges, growing to `MAX_STEP` at an edge and
+ * beyond it, towards the edge it is near. A step is a whole pixel, and at least one while there is
+ * any, since an engine may round a smaller scroll away.
+ */
+function stepAt(position: number, start: number, end: number): number {
+  const toStart = position - start;
+  const toEnd = end - position;
+  if (toStart < ZONE && toStart <= toEnd) {
+    return -Math.ceil(MAX_STEP * clamp((ZONE - toStart) / ZONE, 0, 1));
+  }
+  if (toEnd < ZONE) return Math.ceil(MAX_STEP * clamp((ZONE - toEnd) / ZONE, 0, 1));
+  return 0;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Scrolls an element while a drag holds the pointer near one of its edges (spec phase 6 §3.8): within
+ * 40px of an edge, in a `requestAnimationFrame` loop that scrolls a little more the closer it gets,
+ * 20px a frame at the edge and beyond. The caller says where the pointer is on each move; the loop
+ * goes on under a pointer that rests, and ends when it leaves the zones or when `stop` is called.
+ * The box is read in each frame, so it follows an element that moves. No React: the caller owns when
+ * to start and stop.
+ */
+export function createAutoScroll(
+  element: HTMLElement,
+  options: AutoScrollOptions = {},
+): AutoScroll {
+  const { axis = 'both' } = options;
+  let pointer: { x: number; y: number } | null = null;
+  let frame: number | null = null;
+
+  const steps = () => {
+    if (!pointer) return { x: 0, y: 0 };
+    const box = element.getBoundingClientRect();
+    return {
+      x: axis === 'y' ? 0 : stepAt(pointer.x, box.left, box.right),
+      y: axis === 'x' ? 0 : stepAt(pointer.y, box.top, box.bottom),
+    };
+  };
+
+  const cancel = () => {
+    if (frame !== null) cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
+    frame = null;
+  };
+
+  const run = () => {
+    frame = null;
+    const { x, y } = steps();
+    if (x === 0 && y === 0) return;
+    element.scrollLeft += x;
+    element.scrollTop += y;
+    frame = requestAnimationFrame(run);
+  };
+
+  return {
+    update(x, y) {
+      pointer = { x, y };
+      const { x: dx, y: dy } = steps();
+      if (dx === 0 && dy === 0) cancel();
+      else frame ??= requestAnimationFrame(run);
+    },
+    stop() {
+      pointer = null;
+      cancel();
+    },
+  };
+}

```diff
+
+// Reordering (phase 6 Plan C): the chip and the drop line read a store of their own, so a move of the
+// pointer draws no title, row, body or toolbar. The rows read which column is dragged, which changes
+// twice: they draw at the start of a drag and at its end, and not in between.
+describe('a drag of the title of a column', () => {
+  const POINTER = { pointerId: 1, isPrimary: true, pointerType: 'mouse', button: 0 };
+  const LAYOUT: DataGridColumnLayout = {
+    order: ['id', 'customer', 'qty'],
+    widths: {},
+    hidden: [],
+    pinned: {},
+  };
+  const reset = () => {
+    renders.cell = 0;
+    renders.headerCell = 0;
+    renders.toolbar = 0;
+    renders.body = 0;
+  };
+
+  /** The boxes of a 100px column each, in a 400px frame, with a heading of 40px. */
+  function stubBoxes() {
+    vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockImplementation(function (
+      this: HTMLElement,
+    ) {
+      const cell = this.matches('th.flg-data-grid-head')
+        ? Array.from((this.parentElement as HTMLTableRowElement).cells).indexOf(
+            this as HTMLTableCellElement,
+          )
+        : -1;
+      const left = cell * 100;
+      const bottom = this.matches('.flg-data-grid-frame') ? 400 : 40;
+      const right = cell >= 0 ? left + 100 : 400;
+      return {
+        left: Math.max(left, 0),
+        top: 0,
+        right,
+        bottom,
+        width: right - left,
+        height: bottom,
+      } as DOMRect;
+    });
+    vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'clientWidth', 'get').mockReturnValue(400);
+  }
+
+  function dragQty(props: Partial<React.ComponentProps<typeof DataGrid<Order>>>) {
+    stubBoxes();
+    render(
+      <DataGrid
+        data={ORDERS.slice(0, 5)}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={COLUMNS}
+        caption="Orders"
+        paging={false}
+        {...props}
+      />,
+    );
+    const qty = grid().tHead!.rows[0]!.cells[2]!;
+    reset();
+    fireEvent.pointerDown(qty, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: 250, clientY: 10 });
+    // The first move crosses the threshold: the drag starts, and the rows are told which column it is.
+    fireEvent.pointerMove(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: 140, clientY: 10 });
+    const start = { ...renders };
+    reset();
+    for (const x of [130, 120, 110, 105, 70]) {
+      fireEvent.pointerMove(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: x, clientY: 10 });
+      act(() => {
+        for (const run of frames.splice(0)) run();
+      });
+    }
+    // It did something: the line is at a boundary.
+    expect(document.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-drop-line')).not.toBeNull();
+    const moves = { ...renders };
+    reset();
+    fireEvent.pointerUp(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 0, clientX: 70, clientY: 10 });
+    return { start, moves, release: { ...renders } };
+  }
+
+  it('draws the rows at its start and at its end, and no title, row, body or toolbar for a move', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    const { start, moves, release } = dragQty({ columnLayout: LAYOUT, onColumnLayoutChange });
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    expect(moves).toEqual({ headerCell: 0, toolbar: 0, body: 0, cell: 0 });
+    // Three columns, five rows: the start draws each title and cell once, and the end of a grid whose
+    // parent holds its layout does the same.
+    expect(start).toMatchObject({ headerCell: 3, cell: 15 });
+    expect(release).toMatchObject({ headerCell: 3, cell: 15 });
+  });
+
+  it('draws no more for a grid that holds its own layout, whose state changes once at the release', () => {
+    const { start, moves, release } = dragQty({ onColumnLayoutChange: () => {} });
+    expect(moves).toEqual({ headerCell: 0, toolbar: 0, body: 0, cell: 0 });
+    expect(start.cell).toBeLessThanOrEqual(15);
+    expect(release.cell).toBeLessThanOrEqual(15);
+    expect(release.toolbar).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
+  });
+});
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.reorder.test.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.reorder.test.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a115554
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGrid.reorder.test.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,1038 @@
+import { act, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { useState } from 'react';
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { resetDevWarnings } from '../../internal/warn';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type { DataGridColumn, DataGridColumnLayout, DataGridProps, DataGridState } from './index';
+
+// Reordering the columns (spec phase 6 §3.6, §3.8, §6.3 "Kéo đổi thứ tự"): the drag of a title, the
+// drop line and the chip, the source column that is dimmed, the keys, the announcement, and what the
+// grid sets and takes off while a drag is in flight. What needs a layout engine to be true (the boxes
+// of the line and of the chip, a real mouse, the focus after a move in each engine, no text selected)
+// is proven in the stories (`DataGridColumns.stories.tsx`).
+
+// The animation frames the drag asks for (the coalesced moves, the auto-scroll), run by hand.
+let frames: Map<number, FrameRequestCallback>;
+let nextFrame: number;
+const runFrames = () => {
+  const due = [...frames.values()];
+  frames.clear();
+  act(() => due.forEach((callback) => callback(0)));
+};
+
+const HEAD_HEIGHT = 32;
+const FRAME_HEIGHT = 200;
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  frames = new Map();
+  nextFrame = 1;
+  vi.stubGlobal('requestAnimationFrame', (callback: FrameRequestCallback) => {
+    frames.set(nextFrame, callback);
+    return nextFrame++;
+  });
+  vi.stubGlobal('cancelAnimationFrame', (id: number) => frames.delete(id));
+  // jsdom has no layout, so every element would count as hidden to the code that looks for the
+  // controls of a cell.
+  HTMLElement.prototype.checkVisibility = () => true;
+  // jsdom has no layout. The titles are laid out here from the widths of their captions, in the order
+  // the DOM has them (so a move shows), from x 0; the heading is 32px tall and the frame 200px.
+  vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockImplementation(function (
+    this: HTMLElement,
+  ) {
+    const box = (left: number, top: number, right: number, bottom: number) =>
+      ({
+        left,
+        top,
+        right,
+        bottom,
+        x: left,
+        y: top,
+        width: right - left,
+        height: bottom - top,
+        toJSON: () => ({}),
+      }) as DOMRect;
+    if (this.matches('th.flg-data-grid-head')) {
+      const cells = Array.from((this.parentElement as HTMLTableRowElement).cells);
+      let left = 0;
+      for (const cell of cells) {
+        const width = WIDTH_OF[cell.textContent ?? ''] ?? 0;
+        if (cell === this) return box(left, 0, left + width, HEAD_HEIGHT);
+        left += width;
+      }
+    }
+    if (this.matches('thead, thead > tr')) return box(0, 0, 504, HEAD_HEIGHT);
+    if (this.matches('.flg-data-grid-frame')) return box(0, 0, 504, FRAME_HEIGHT);
+    if (this.matches('.flg-data-grid-main')) return box(0, 0, 504, FRAME_HEIGHT);
+    return box(0, 0, 0, 0);
+  });
+  // The box the line is placed in is drawn at its own size.
+  vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'offsetWidth', 'get').mockImplementation(function (
+    this: HTMLElement,
+  ) {
+    return this.matches('.flg-data-grid-main') ? 504 : 0;
+  });
+  // The frame shows what its rectangle says.
+  for (const [name, value] of [
+    ['clientWidth', 504],
+    ['clientHeight', FRAME_HEIGHT],
+  ] as const) {
+    vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, name, 'get').mockReturnValue(value);
+  }
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'checkVisibility');
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'showPopover');
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'hidePopover');
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+  vi.useRealTimers();
+  document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-flg-grid-cursor');
+});
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  qty: number;
+  total: number;
+}
+
+const ORDERS: Order[] = [
+  { id: 'DH-1030', customer: 'Nguyễn Minh', qty: 4, total: 1250000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1029', customer: 'Trần Hải', qty: 1, total: 890000 },
+  { id: 'DH-1028', customer: 'Lê An', qty: 12, total: 15400000 },
+];
+
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+  { field: 'total', caption: 'Total', dataType: 'number', width: 120 },
+];
+const WIDTH_OF: Record<string, number> = { Order: 104, Customer: 200, Qty: 80, Total: 120 };
+const ORDER = ['id', 'customer', 'qty', 'total'];
+
+function Orders(props: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>>) {
+  return (
+    <DataGrid
+      data={ORDERS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={false}
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+/** A grid whose parent keeps the layout, as a caller that saves it does. */
+function Controlled({
+  onChange,
+  keep = true,
+  ...props
+}: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>> & {
+  onChange: (layout: DataGridColumnLayout) => void;
+  keep?: boolean;
+}) {
+  const [layout, setLayout] = useState<DataGridColumnLayout>({
+    order: ORDER,
+    widths: {},
+    hidden: [],
+    pinned: {},
+  });
+  return (
+    <Orders
+      columnLayout={layout}
+      onColumnLayoutChange={(next) => {
+        onChange(next);
+        if (keep) setLayout(next);
+      }}
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+const grid = () => screen.getByRole('grid') as HTMLTableElement;
+// The titles of the columns: the filler column's is none.
+const titles = () =>
+  Array.from(grid().tHead!.rows[0]!.cells).filter(
+    (cell) => !cell.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-filler'),
+  );
+const captions = () => titles().map((cell) => cell.textContent);
+const title = (name: string) => titles().find((cell) => cell.textContent?.includes(name))!;
+const chip = () => document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-drag-chip');
+const line = () => document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-drop-line');
+const html = () => document.documentElement;
+const region = () => document.querySelector('[aria-live="polite"]')!;
+const dimmed = () => grid().querySelectorAll('[data-drag-source]');
+// The live region says it a tick after: the timers are the test's, and the frames stay the stub's.
+const fakeTimers = () => vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout'] });
+const tick = () => act(() => void vi.advanceTimersByTime(0));
+
+const POINTER = { pointerId: 1, isPrimary: true, pointerType: 'mouse', button: 0 };
+const press = (element: Element, x: number, y = 10, init: PointerEventInit = {}) =>
+  fireEvent.pointerDown(element, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: x, clientY: y, ...init });
+// A move with the main button down, as every move of a press is.
+const move = (x: number, y = 10, init: PointerEventInit = {}) =>
+  fireEvent.pointerMove(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 1, clientX: x, clientY: y, ...init });
+const release = (x: number, y = 10) =>
+  fireEvent.pointerUp(document, { ...POINTER, buttons: 0, clientX: x, clientY: y });
+
+/** A drag of the title `name` to the pointer at `x`, `y`, released there. */
+function drag(name: string, x: number, y = 10) {
+  const from = title(name);
+  press(from, 400);
+  move(x, y);
+  runFrames();
+  release(x, y);
+}
+
+// The keys of the platform: ⌘ on Apple and Ctrl elsewhere.
+const apple = () => vi.spyOn(navigator, 'platform', 'get').mockReturnValue('MacIntel');
+const windows = () => vi.spyOn(navigator, 'platform', 'get').mockReturnValue('Win32');
+const modShift = { ctrlKey: true, shiftKey: true };
+
+describe('dragging a title', () => {
+  it('moves the column to the boundary the pointer is nearest to, with one onColumnLayoutChange', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    render(<Orders onColumnLayoutChange={onColumnLayoutChange} onStateChange={onStateChange} />);
+    // Total is 384..504; the boundary between Order and Customer is at 104.
+    drag('Total', 110);
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    const layout: DataGridColumnLayout = {
+      order: ['id', 'total', 'customer', 'qty'],
+      widths: { id: 104, customer: 200, qty: 80, total: 120 },
+      hidden: [],
+      pinned: {},
+    };
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith(layout);
+    expect(onStateChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    expect(onStateChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
+      expect.objectContaining({ columnLayout: layout }),
+      'columnLayout',
+    );
+    expect(captions()).toEqual(['Order', 'Total', 'Customer', 'Qty']);
+  });
+
+  it('moves a column to the start and to the end', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    render(<Orders onColumnLayoutChange={onColumnLayoutChange} />);
+    drag('Qty', 5);
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange.mock.lastCall![0].order).toEqual([
+      'qty',
+      'id',
+      'customer',
+      'total',

+describe('the frame that scrolls under the pointer', () => {
+  it('is scrolled sideways only, while the pointer is near its edge, and no more once the drag is over', () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    const frame = grid().parentElement as HTMLElement;
+    frame.scrollLeft = 0;
+    press(title('Customer'), 200);
+    move(500);
+    runFrames();
+    expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBeGreaterThan(0);
+    const scrolled = frame.scrollLeft;
+    release(500);
+    runFrames();
+    expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBe(scrolled);
+    expect(frames.size).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it('works out the line again when the frame scrolls under a pointer that rests', () => {
+    render(<Orders />);
+    const frame = grid().parentElement as HTMLElement;
+    press(title('Total'), 400);
+    move(110);
+    runFrames();
+    expect(line()!.style.left).toBe('102px');
+    // The columns move 50px left under the pointer: the boundary at 104 is now at 54, the next at 254.
+    vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockImplementation(function (
+      this: HTMLElement,
+    ) {
+      const base = {
+        top: 0,
+        bottom: HEAD_HEIGHT,
+        x: 0,
+        y: 0,
+        width: 0,
+        height: 0,
+        toJSON: () => ({}),
+      };
+      if (this.matches('th.flg-data-grid-head')) {
+        const cells = Array.from((this.parentElement as HTMLTableRowElement).cells);
+        let left = -50;
+        for (const cell of cells) {
+          const width = WIDTH_OF[cell.textContent ?? ''] ?? 0;
+          if (cell === this) return { ...base, left, right: left + width } as DOMRect;
+          left += width;
+        }
+      }
+      if (this.matches('.flg-data-grid-frame, .flg-data-grid-main')) {
+        return { ...base, left: 0, right: 504, bottom: FRAME_HEIGHT } as DOMRect;
+      }
+      if (this.matches('thead, thead > tr')) return { ...base, left: 0, right: 504 } as DOMRect;
+      return { ...base, left: 0, right: 504 } as DOMRect;
+    });
+    act(() => {
+      frame.dispatchEvent(new Event('scroll'));
+    });
+    expect(line()!.style.left).toBe('52px');
+    release(110);
+  });
+});

+    press('ArrowRight');

+      'id',
+      'qty',
+      'total',

+    ]);
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange.mock.lastCall![0].hidden).toEqual(['qty']);

+  it('says where the column went', () => {
+    fakeTimers();
+    render(<Orders />);

+    tick();

+  });

+  it('uses Ctrl on a PC and ⌘ on a Mac, and not the other', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    windows();

+    press('ArrowRight', { metaKey: true, shiftKey: true });

+    press('ArrowRight');

+    render(<Orders onColumnLayoutChange={onColumnLayoutChange} />);

+    press('ArrowRight');
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    press('ArrowRight', { metaKey: true, shiftKey: true });
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
+  });
+
+  it('wants exactly those modifiers: no Alt, and Shift', () => {
+    const onColumnLayoutChange = vi.fn();
+    windows();
+    render(<Orders onColumnLayoutChange={onColumnLayoutChange} />);

+    press('ArrowRight', { ctrlKey: true });
+    press('ArrowRight', { shiftKey: true });

+    press('ArrowRight', { ctrlKey: true, shiftKey: true, metaKey: true });
+    expect(onColumnLayoutChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('is not for the cell of a row or the title of the column of boxes', () => {
```
